The microwave oven: an equivalent power balance, done safely Safety first. Never connect the VNA, a TinySA or any probe to the oven's antenna, waveguide or cavity. Never put rods, spheres or any metal inside a running oven. Never run it empty. Receive only, from outside, through an attenuator. The oven page has the full safety list. You cannot do the VNA two-port balance on an oven, because it is its own source. The equivalent pieces are: What the magnetron delivers: water calorimetry in the cavity, P = m c ΔT / t, with m in kg, c = 4186 J/(kg·K). A 1 kg load heated 10 K in 60 s corresponds to about 700 W (calculator E). Water-load calorimetry is the usual way to estimate oven output; a formal standard procedure exists (IEC 60705), so check its exact method before quoting any figure. What leaks to the receiver: a receive-only 3/4 in sphere into a spectrum analyzer, through a fixed attenuator, at a fixed geometry. Record the level in dBm; convert to mW. Without a calibrated antenna this is a relative number. Use channel power across 2.40 to 2.50 GHz, not a single bin, because the magnetron frequency wanders. What the rods do: the same rod scan as the other bands, now on the leaked signal. Fit κ and compare with the sphere-transmitter κ at 2.45 GHz and with the brass versus W1 ratio. Limit: this never gives the leaked fraction of the magnetron output, only changes in a relative level. Oven output varies with power setting (duty cycling), load and line voltage, so run at full power with a fixed load and repeat. E. Calorimetry and dBm conversions Water mass (kg) Temperature rise (K) Time (s) Analyzer reading (dBm) Attenuator plus cable loss ahead of the analyzer (dB) Compute Defaults are placeholders, not measurements. 10. Limits and how this could fail A good fit to T = exp(-κ cos²φ) is expected from ordinary physics. It is not a detection. If brass and W1 give the same κ and κ does not scale as 1/f, the literal Joule reading is out. That is a useful result. If the TX sphere rotated 90° moves the curve, the loss is tied to the transmitter's polarisation, as for an ordinary wave. The VNA phase and amplitude drift with temperature and cable movement; repeat runs and keep raw data. Near-field coupling, plate effects and the acrylic's dielectric loss all show up in S21. The plates-only baseline removes some of them. Everything labelled "proposal" (closed-box balance, thresholds, stub lengths at 2.45 GHz) is untested. 11. Sources C. Monstein and J. P. Wesley, Europhys. Lett. 59(4), 514 (2002), Eq. 7 to 9, Fig. 3. Summarised in joule-loss-positions and loss-modes. Fixture position: Monstein and Wesley give no polarizer position ("intervening", abstract; Fig. 2 shows the rotatable 3 x 3 array on a chair). Butterworth, Allison, Cavazos and Mullen, J. Sci. Explor. 27(1), 13 (2013), p. 15: "Between Tx and Rx are positioned a pair of rotatable polarizer-analyzer arrays"; p. 16: "nine wires in 3 x 3 arrays, a half-wavelength long and a quarter-wave apart, one horizontal and one vertical". Hub rod loss and thermal model: rod-thermal (S0, S1, S1-capped, S2 readings; microkelvin heating). Material constants: Aviva Metals (C36000 data sheet); MakeItFrom (C36000, hardened W1); EngMats (C80W1); the hub's rod-thermal page (MetalZenith, MatWeb, copper.org). Values differ between suppliers, so treat them as uncertain by a few tens of percent. Skin effect and dipole loss resistance: C. A. Balanis, Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design (conductor loss of a dipole, RL proportional to length / wire circumference × Rs). Oven leakage limit 5 mW/cm² at 5 cm: 21 CFR 1030.10 (as cited on the hub's rod-thermal page). Oven rating by water load: IEC 60705 (not consulted).

description: Planned shared submersible field kit: one TX Pelican cube for both antennas, lid-open RX case, sequential TinySA use, ballast, IP67 depth honesty. Not a claim it has been built.
text: Shared field kit · planned end-state · not yet built One TX Pelican, one RX case, two electrically separate antennas Cargo plan for taking Experiment A (1296 MHz sleeve-stub + pancake) and Experiment B (433.59 MHz balls + rods) into the field. Plastic cube = hydrostatic shell. RadioScreen = Faraday. The antennas share a box, not an RF feed. This page is not a claim the hull has been bought, ballasted, or dunked. Pelican 1200 on setup.html#shop stays the small TinySA / coil travel case. It is not this submersible TX hull. Cage pancake protocol stays on setup.html. 433 parts stay on monstein.html / sphere.html. TX: one cubical watertight case One cube. Cutout foam holds the 1296 sleeve-stub sled and the 433 TX sphere in separate wells. The whole inner pack is wrapped in RadioScreen. Plastic Pelican = hydrostatic shell; mesh = Faraday. Flat sides of the cube are for aiming the stub axis; do not rely on a round case for that. Antennas are cargo in one Faraday wrap — they keep their own feeds. Do not tee 1296 and 433 onto one coax. 23 cm BPF stays in the 1296 TX chain inside the wrap (setup.html#bpf). Experiment B ball: coax into the sphere, outer as shield, no balun (monstein.html#parts). RX: second case, usually lid open The receiver case is not the submerged article. Leave the lid open. Drape a RadioScreen mesh tent over the instruments so Dan can read two TinySA screens (one at 1296, one at 433) through the see-through mesh. Same “no USB out on a sealed run” honesty as the bench tents: if a cable is out, it is a leaky config. Sequential is the default Dan has three TinySA Ultra units now. Sequential (one experiment at a time) is the default. Mode TinySA count Notes Sequential TX+RX 2 One pair. Switch the antennas / wells between A and B. Default. Sequential with a spare 3 (what he has) Two dedicated to the live experiment; third as spare or a switched TX. Simultaneous dedicated 4 TX1296, TX433, RX1296, RX433. Only if they don’t interfere and a 4th Ultra is bought. With 3, one TX is switched or shared. Simultaneous is optional later, not the first field plan. Harmonic warning (why sequential first) 1296 / 3 = 432 MHz, only 1.59 MHz from 433.59. 433.59 × 3 = 1300.77 MHz vs 1296. Square-wave / mixer-region TinySA drive is already harmonic-rich. If you ever run both transmitters at once you need: 23 cm BPF on the 1296 TX (already in the A chain) a 70 cm BPF on the 433 TX separate foam wells both antennas still inside the mesh Do sequential first. Do not treat a simultaneous dunk as the first article. Ballast — the empty cube floats Pelican 0340 buoyancy is 220 lb. The empty cube floats. Do not drill the hull (kills IP67, seal, and warranty). Pelican cubes have no D-rings. Ballast path: NRS 1″ HD cam straps through the four fold-down handles, then lead or steel shot bags on that webbing. No hull holes. Do not use VHB pad-eyes as the primary seawater path. Depth honesty IP67 = 1 m / 30 min, not continuous seawater. First tests: pool / shallow Florida. Later seawater is a separate, logged step — different risk, different log row, not implied by buying a cube. Literature adjacent to later seawater: Tomilin, Lukin & Gulkov (2021) marine-channel / spherical-antenna field experiment (~470 m seawater; contested vs Maxwell attenuation) — cited on p. 31 of Hively’s close-hold manuscript. Hub card + DOI: library.html#tomilin-2021 · doi.org/10.1134/S1063785021060146. Educational pointer only — not a claim this kit has been dunked or that a marine link is settled physics. Gap list vs Exp A/B: #tomilin-gaps. Tomilin 2021 vs Experiments A & B — what we still omit for a later at-sea article Scope: land-first Exp A (1296 MHz ¾″ sphere / mesh) and Exp B (433.59 MHz balls + polarizer rods). Dan’s Nanuk (and Pelican) cases are for land outdoor use — they are not Tomilin-class continuous-seawater enclosures. A future marine replication is a separate logged article, not implied by buying land cases or the planned plastic cube below. Tomilin 2021 Hub Exp A / B today Still needed for Tomilin-like sea test 27.4 MHz HF radio (~1.17 W) A: 1296 MHz TinySA class; B: 433.59 MHz Licensed HF path (or explicit scale study) — not a drop-in of A/B RF Tesla spiral Ø320 mm + rod + Cu sphere Ø60 mm; dielectric jacket vs seawater SMA bulkhead into hollow Al ball (A ¾″ / B 2.50″); no Tesla coil Spiral + rod feed + full dielectric cladding; B’s 2.50″ OD is closest to 60 mm Sealed metal box (radio + batteries) rigidly on antenna; RX → voice recorder in box Nanuk/Pelican land cases; mesh tents; TinySA on bench Pressure-rated seawater hulls, wet-mate glands, submerged recorder/telemetry — not Nanuk land cases Nylon ropes; buoy 6 m / tow 4 m; GPS 20–470 m; σ, T logged Land rails / precision ranging notes (A, B) GPS + depth sensors; nylon buoy/tow; seawater conductivity/temp log No polarizer-rod cube underwater B rods = land MW polarizer only Keep rods out of the seawater Tesla–sphere article unless a separate B-on-boat control Library card (figures + citations): library.html#tomilin-2021. PDF: papers/…Marine-Radio-Channel.pdf. Contested physics — educational planning only. A metal case is optional later (Faraday + hull in one) but corrosion, no see-through, and true subsea boxes (Slayson IP68 aluminum, Blue Robotics watertight-box class) are small and expensive. First buy: plastic cube + internal mesh. Those metal/subsea boxes are “too small / later,” not the first SKU. Case SKUs (vendor pages ~Sep 2026) Prices are what the vendor pages showed around Sep 2026. Confirm before you buy. Not an endorsement beyond “this is the SKU we checked.” Case Role Notes Pelican 0340 Protector Cube SKU 0340-000-110 pelican.com/…/protector/0340 FIRST BUY TX hull (and a second cube if you want a matching lid-open RX shell) ~$479.95 foam / $424.95 empty (~Sep 2026). Same plastic-cube + internal-mesh idea. Pelican 0370 Cube pelican.com/…/protector/0370 Largest cube in this family ~$589.95 foam / $539.95 empty. Interior 24×24×24 in. IP67. PP. Pick N Pluck. Not required if 0340 fits. Pelican 1200 with pick-n-pluck foam (link stays on setup.html#shop) Small TinySA / coil travel case Not the submersible TX hull. Do not rebrand the 1200 as the cube. Slayson IP68 aluminum / Blue Robotics watertight box class Too small / later True subsea boxes. Corrosion, no see-through, expensive, small. Not the first SKU. Not first buy (one-liners): Nanuk 960 ~$375 rectangle; SKB 3i-2217-12; B&W Type 5500 cheaper near-cube; Zarges K470 aluminum is IP54 on the US 40564 SKU / IP67 EU 380366 — metal cages the RF unless antennas are outside on glands; Blue Robotics WTE is a cylinder; Hammond 1554 / Hoffman Al too small or not 6P. Summary on the master page: index.html#kit. Tekbox TBPS01 · H20 / H10 / H5 / E5 near-field probes (on hand · Sep 2026) Dan’s set (often labeled “TEXBOX” on the box) is the Tekbox TBPS01 EMC near-field probe kit: magnetic-field loops H20 (20 mm), H10 (10 mm), H5 (5 mm), and electric tip E5 (5 mm), SMB connectors, ~75 cm SMB→SMA cable, coupling plots, and a certificate / measurement plots (keep with the wooden case). Official manual: TBPS01 / TBWA2 manual (PDF) · Paper certificate/plots stay with the wooden case (scan kept locally on the assistant machine). · product: tekbox.com TBPS01. Frequency class: coupling characterized roughly 30 kHz–6 GHz (see probe plots; H20 has noted resonances near ~1.3 GHz and ~4 GHz). Hively B-field null (required for SLW/SW vs TEM language). Dr. Hively’s guidance (and IARD_2020 / earlier notes, including the 2016 patent-era configurations where B was not found): when a sphere (Exp A or B) or other detector shows a candidate Scalar Longitudinal Wave (SLW) or Scalar Wave (SW) signature, place a magnetic-field (H) probe near the receiver and look for the presence or absence of B at the same time / band. A credible “we detected SLW or SW, not TEM” claim needs that B knowledge — TEM carries a magnetic field; ideal SLW (B=0, E∥k, C≠0) and SW (E=B=0, C≠0) bookkeeping do not. Warm skepticism: a quiet H-probe is necessary supporting evidence, not by itself a proof of SLW/SW. Probe Type Tip / loop Use on this hub H20 H-field 20 mm loop First B-null survey near Exp A/B spheres (most sensitive of the three H tips) H10 H-field 10 mm loop Narrower localization if H20 sees something H5 H-field 5 mm loop Finest localization / PCB-scale; also useful near SMA bulkheads E5 E-field 5 mm tip Corroborate electric pickup near the sphere; not a substitute for the H-null B-null protocol (anytime measuring for SLW / SW) Run the sphere listen (TinySA Ultra on Exp A and/or B SMA) and mark the candidate frequency / time window. Without changing the RF scene, connect H20 (then H10/H5 if needed) via SMB→SMA to the same TinySA (or a second Ultra). Use a ~21 dB TinySA LNA (or TBWA2) when the bare reading is near the noise floor — log gain. Expected levels: #tinysa-expected. Hold the H-loop near the receiving sphere (and scan orientations: loop plane parallel / perpendicular to expected B). Keep hands off the shield; Tekbox loops are designed to reject common-mode from the hand. Interpret (educational): Sphere excess + H-probe at noise → consistent with non-TEM / weak-B hypothesis (SLW/SW language still needs full null suite). Sphere excess + clear H-probe line → treat as TEM or mixed; do not claim pure SLW/SW. Neither → no detection claim. Log probe model, orientation, distance to sphere, TinySA RBW/LNA, and whether polarizing rods were present (Exp B). For Exodus / Faraday-cage listens, see Experiment E listen checklist. Expected TinySA Ultra response (order-of-magnitude) Use Tekbox’s absolute curves (manual Picture 2 / 3), not the faint certificate “coupling loss” VNA prints: H-probes are output power [dBm] at 1 µT; E5 is output power [dBm] at 1 V/m. That dBm is what TinySA Ultra shows into 50 Ω (before cable loss). Numbers below are eyeballed from the manual (±~5 dB). Certificate serial for this kit: TBPS0121231 (cal 05 Aug 2026) — good as “this set passed,” poor for digitizing faint traces. Probe ~433 MHz (bare) ~1.3 GHz (bare) + ~21 dB TinySA amp @433 + ~21 dB amp @1.3 GHz H20 @ 1 µT about −5 to 0 dBm about −15 to −25 dBm (H20 dip near ~1.2 GHz) +16 to +21 dBm −4 to +6 dBm H10 @ 1 µT about −15 to −20 dBm about −5 to −12 dBm +1 to +6 dBm +9 to +16 dBm H5 @ 1 µT about −28 to −35 dBm about −15 to −22 dBm −7 to −14 dBm −1 to +6 dBm E5 @ 1 V/m about −55 to −65 dBm about −45 to −55 dBm −34 to −44 dBm −24 to −34 dBm Caution notes. Voltage: Tekbox warning — do not use these probes on conductors above 75 V DC or 50 V AC. Fine beside a Faraday case for B-null; not for poking a 600 V capacitor stack. Real fields are often weaker: table assumes 1 µT / 1 V/m at the tip. Cage leakage is often ≪ that, so TinySA may sit near the noise floor even with the amp. Amp: Dan’s TinySA Ultra ~21 dB LNAs (three on hand) slide every reading up by ~21 dB. Use when bare probe @433 is below about −80 to −90 dBm; log LNA on/off. Optional Tekbox TBWA2 if present — same idea, log gain. Cable: subtract ~1–2 dB for a short SMA jumper. Certificate vs manual: certificate = faint S21 coupling-loss plots (relative). Manual Picture 2/3 = absolute dBm vs frequency — use those for TinySA expectations. Manual PDF: TBPS01 / TBWA2. title: Lab
headings: Faraday-cage replication of Hively US 9,306,527 at 1.3 GHz
description: 1.3 GHz Faraday-cage replication of Hively US 9,306,527 with HAM legal box and CSV log.
text: Lab · 1.3 GHz · not 8 GHz Faraday-cage replication of Hively US 9,306,527 at 1.3 GHz Different experiment (not this mesh/copper enclosure): Monstein–Wesley 2002 brass-rod polarizer — monstein.html. Experiment A’s first-article radiator is now the ¾″ KB-1820 sphere — setup.html#sphere-a. Scale the IARD 2020 copper-enclosure idea down in frequency to the 23 cm amateur band, where a licensed operator can use a legal source. The hypothesis under test is whether a detector outside a copper box (¾″ sphere first article; bifilar or plasma as optional controls) still sees a coherent tone when TEM leakage is beaten down by many skin depths. A null is a successful experiment. HAM legal box — 23 cm (1240–1300 MHz). Transmitting in this band requires a valid amateur radio license and compliance with Part 97 (US) or your administration’s rules: identification, band edges, power, spurious emissions, and coordination. 1296 MHz is the weak-signal calling frequency — do not park a continuous unattended carrier there. Prefer a quiet segment, identify, and listen first. This lab uses a licensed 23 cm source into RG-405 — no magnetron, no microwave oven, no 8 GHz TWT as the primary source. Copper skin-depth table δ = 1 / √(π f μ σ) μ = μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ H/m σ_Cu ≈ 5.8×10⁷ S/m Computed (not copied). 2885 skin depths is a “many δ” Faraday target used on earlier Britton pages; ⅛ in (3.175 mm) copper is ~1733 δ at 1.3 GHz and ~4297 δ at 8 GHz. Live δ at slider frequency: —. Lab default 1.300 GHz. f Frequency δ (copper) 10 δ 100 δ 1000 δ 2885 δ Classical TEM power attenuation through a wall is on the order of e−2t/δ (plus aperture leakage). If a detector still hears the tone through a sealed, many-δ box and the TEM-antenna negative control is quiet, you have an anomaly worth publishing. If it does not, that is also worth publishing. Hand-wind BOM Item Qty / notes K-Mac KB-1820 ¾″ Al hollow sphere, RG-405U pin-hole feed First-article radiator/detector at 1296.000 MHz (fed by RG-405U, centre conductor soldered into a #76 pin hole, shield kept off the ball (corrected 5 Oct 2026, exp-1296.html#feed)). Ships with no hole — shop drills. See setup.html#sphere-a · #sma-shop-a. RG-405/U semi-rigid + SMA or Type N (archived control) Optional sleeve-balun stub path only — setup.html#archive-bifilar / #sleeve. λ = 231.3 mm; λ/4 sleeve = 57.8 mm; stub λ/10 = 23.1 mm. Copper/brass thin-wall tube for sleeve (archived) Optional control only; ID clears 0.086″ with only a thin gap Magnet wire 22 AWG (18–26 OK) (archived bifilar) Optional control: one strand folded in half (~2.2 m). See #archive-bifilar. Not the first article. Non-magnetic former (acrylic / PLA / PVC) (archived) Optional pancake former ≈ 35 mm OD. Cricut StandardGrip winding jig is archived — #archive-bifilar. Copper box / tube + lids Wall ≥ 1 mm preferred (≈ 546 δ at 1.3 GHz). ⅛ in is luxurious. All seams soldered or RF-gasketed. Feed-through only via filtered bulkhead. Licensed 23 cm source Transverter, brick, or amateur radio; attenuators; directional coupler. Identify on air if the stub radiates outside the box. Dummy load 50 Ω, 23 cm rated Negative control TEM reference antenna Small dipole or loop outside the box — the “should go away when sealed” channel Optional N–Z detector U-shaped CFL / neon + isolated DC bias, axis ∥ expected k Optional N–Z Tx 7-inch galvanized stovepipe TM01, 69 cm guide + 69 cm probe, 5.8 cm choke, Type N + 3 dB pad (QEX 2011) SA / VNA / SDR, LNA, 1:1 balun Record RBW, NF, averaging. On hand: TinySA Ultra (SA/gen) + NanoRFE VNA6000-A (S11/S21/TDR) — kit.html#vna6000 Leakage / field probe Confirm TEM is actually down when the lid is on Fixture + travel kit (do not fork SKUs here) Acrylic/HDPE plates, nylon hardware, <10 cm SMA pigtail, RadioScreen, conductive hook-and-loop, Pelican 1200 foam — verified links on Setup shopping list. First article: mount Amphenol 901-9875 SMA bulkheads on two K-Mac KB-1820 ¾″ spheres (shop clearance — ships with no hole). setup.html#sphere-a · #sma-shop-a. Place matching spheres in TX and RX RadioScreen tents (or copper-box article: bulkhead into the box). Distance r = sphere-to-sphere or bulkhead tip to tip. Precision rail / NF floors: setup.html#ranging-a (Exp A); Exp B: monstein.html#ranging-b. Rods are Exp B only. Mesh-tent article: RadioScreen cages as in Setup — removable flap seals (conductive hook-and-loop / clips / magnets), not a permanent copper-tape weld. Do not mix mesh vs copper-box cage types in one CSV without labeling. Archived optional control (not first article): Cricket/Cricut sticky-mat bifilar + sleeve-stub — setup.html#archive-bifilar. If used, label detector bifilar and keep that path out of the primary sphere log rows. Run the control matrix below. Log every row. Do not peek only at the “interesting” condition. Pack the same kit for Lady Lake, FL then Middletown, RI (packing checklist). Transmitter ¾″ sphere (primary for this lab) K-Mac KB-1820 ¾″ Al hollow sphere, driven by a licensed 23 cm source. The sphere is the driven element: fed by RG-405U, centre conductor soldered into a #76 pin hole, shield kept off the ball (corrected 5 Oct 2026, exp-1296.html#feed). Unlike Experiment B, the shield must not touch the ball. Build: setup.html#sphere-a. Archived control: RG-405 sleeve-balun stub — #archive-bifilar / #sleeve (patent education kept; not the first article). N–Z-style (optional companion) Zimmerman QEX 2011: 7-inch stovepipe TM01, λcut ≈ 23.23 cm, 69 cm guide + 69 cm longitudinal probe, 5.8 cm choke collar, Type N + 3 dB pad, U-tube fluorescent detector. Same frequency family, different launch. Do not mix data sets without labeling Tx type. Control matrix (run all of them) Code Configuration What it is for open Box open or lid off; stub visible Positive TEM+whatever baseline slotted Lid on but a defined slot / incomplete seam Aperture leakage scaling sealed Lid on, seams RF-tight, only filtered feed-through The actual Faraday test dummy_load Source into a 50 Ω load instead of the stub (same cables, same box) Kills the antenna; leftover = conducted / pickup 90deg Detector rotated 90° (coil edge-on, or plasma axis ⊥ k) Orientation / polarization control tem_negative Ordinary small dipole/loop in place of the sphere (or archived bifilar/plasma), same r, same sealed box If TEM antenna is dead and sphere (or bifilar) is live, you have a fork in the data; if both live, you have a leak Also record: source off; modulation off; detector disconnected (terminate); 90° box rotation; distance sweep. Prefer lock-in or a known AM/CW ID so you are not integrating birdies. CSV schema and in-page log Columns (stable): timestamp, run_id, config, f_MHz, P_dBm, r_m, orientation_deg, cage_state, detector, reading_dBm, notes. config and cage_state should use the codes above. detector: sphere (first article) | bifilar (archived control) | plasma | tem_dipole | tem_loop. Stored in this browser until you export. run_id config f_MHz P_dBm r_m orientation_deg cage_state detector reading_dBm notes Add row Export CSV Clear log # timestamp run_id config f_MHz P_dBm r_m deg cage detector reading notes Publishing checklist License class, call sign, frequency, and that 1296 calling was not occupied by an unidentified carrier. Photographs of sphere + SMA install, box/mesh seams, and (if used) archived sleeve/pancake fixtures. VNA6000-A S11 of sphere feed (and archived sleeve-stub if run); export S2P when it matters; note detector type in the CSV. Uses by experiment: kit.html#vna6000. Complete control matrix, not a highlight reel. Source-off and dummy-load rows. TEM-antenna negative control at the same r and RBW. Distance sweep (even 0.3–3 m) plotted; state whether it looks like 1/r or a leak resonance. Box wall thickness in mm and in skin depths at the operating frequency (use the table). Raw CSV plus instrument screenshots with timestamps. A one-sentence claim that matches the data: “sealed − dummy ≥ X dB” or “no excess above dummy.” Cite US 9,306,527, IARD 2020, and (if used) Zimmerman QEX 2011. State that SLW is not settled physics. Safety RF: 23 cm can cook eyes and fingers at surprisingly modest power in the near field. Know your ERP, use attenuators, keep people out of the stub’s near zone, and never look into an open waveguide. Soldering: flux fumes, lead (if any), hot copper boxes. Do not cook a sealed cage: a driven antenna inside a closed conducting box dissipates power in the walls and the feed. Watch temperature; do not apply oven-like power; provide a load path (dummy-load control exists for a reason). No magnetron. No modified microwave oven in this protocol. GFCI on mains instruments. Discharge bias supplies on plasma tubes before handling.

title: Learn
headings: Classical baseline (what they all say is incomplete)
What each says Maxwell is missing
How the detectors are supposed to work
description: Nikolova–Zimmerman vs Hively vs Meyl briefing with accurate citations.
text: Learn Briefing: three vocabularies for “not TEM” Nikolova–Zimmerman, Hively, and Meyl do not say the same thing. They start from different missing terms, build different hardware, and should be cited separately. This page is a map, not a verdict. SLW / longitudinal-A / potential-vortex claims are active research and fringe relative to textbook CED. Treat every number below as literature or illustration unless you measure it. Classical baseline (what they all say is incomplete) Textbook Maxwell–Heaviside in SI: ∇·D = ρ ∇·B = 0 ∇×E = −∂B/∂t ∇×H = J + ∂D/∂t Potentials that automatically satisfy the homogeneous pair: B = ∇×A E = −∇Φ − ∂A/∂t The Lorenz leftover, usually set to zero as a gauge condition rather than as a Maxwell equation: C ≡ ∇·A + (1/c²) ∂Φ/∂t (Lorenz gauge: C = 0) Free-space communications waves are TEM: E ⊥ k, H ⊥ k, S = E×H ∥ k. A metal wall attenuates TEM over a skin depth δ = 1 / √(π f μ σ) copper σ ≈ 5.8×10⁷ S/m, μ = μ₀ At 1.300 GHz, δ_Cu ≈ 1.833 µm. At 8 GHz, δ_Cu ≈ 0.739 µm. Faraday cages work for TEM when walls are many skin depths and holes ≪ λ. Whether a longitudinal / potential channel ignores that attenuation is the experimental question — not a theorem of this webpage. Three programs N–Z Physical A, TM01 launch Engineers treat A as auxiliary; this line treats longitudinal A as measurable (macroscopic Aharonov–Bohm). Tx: monopole in a circular waveguide below TEM cutoff (TM01-like). Rx: DC-biased plasma / fluorescent U-tube aligned with k. Signature: reversing bias reverses RF phase. Detected RF power is argued to come from the local bias supply, not TEM Poynting flux. Am = μ₀ Im / (2π k₀ r) IRMS = R · Am/√2 R ≈ 1.86×10⁵–2.64×10⁵ m/H Hively Keep C; B≈0 SLW Does not throw out E and B. Promotes C to a dynamical field. SLW: B≈0, C≠0, longitudinal E along ∇C. Tx: linear monopole + λ/4 skirt balun forcing irrotational (gradient-driven) current JL=∇κ. Rx: bifilar pancake, adjacent turns opposing, net B≈0, face-on to EL. Patent claim: unconstrained by classical skin effect. Prad = I²/(4π) · √(μ/ε) = I² Z / (4π) (US 9,306,527 Eq. 15) Meyl Potential vortex τ₂ Starts from Faraday and adds a relaxation term B/τ₂. “Scalar wave” here is a longitudinal E-structure whose speed is not locked at c in his reading. Hardware: paired Tesla pancakes, spheres, LED-in-a-box kits. Bruhn (JSE) argued the scalar-wave condition plus source-free Maxwell leaves no oscillating wave. Over-unity and v>c are claims, not defaults in this hub. What each says Maxwell is missing Nikolova–Zimmerman Hively EED / SLW Meyl Incomplete piece Treating A as gauge fiction Forcing Lorenz leftover C=0 Irrotational-E axiom; ∇·B=0 New object Longitudinal A∥ (TM01-like) C as a field; EL, JL Potential vortex; τ₂ Wave A∥ ejωt k̂, speed c B=0, C≠0, E∥∇C, speed c Longitudinal E-structure, speed free (claimed) Cage / metal Ordinary metals miss A∥; plasma sees momentum kick No classical skin δ for SLW (hypothesis) Fast vortices “tunnel” Energy at RX From detector bias, not TEM Poynting Extra CE terms; continuity may fail briefly Can exceed TX (claimed; not used here) Typical hardware ~1.3 GHz coax/circular TM01, neon/CFL Monopole + skirt, bifilar, VNA S21 Tesla pancakes, spheres, LED boards Mainstream status QEX + JAP exist; interpretation disputed Patent issued; Physics Essays / IARD; not IEEE EMC University restrictions; kit literature How the detectors are supposed to work Plasma U-tube (N–Z) Core sentence from the original explainer: free electrons in a low-pressure plasma have high mobility; an incident longitudinal AL couples to kinetic momentum and modulates drift velocity along the tube, producing RF current on the bias circuit. pmech = mv = pcan − qA In metal, induced RF velocity is argued to be millimetres per second; in a fluorescent plasma, tens of metres per second. Orient the long axis ∥ k. Reverse DC bias → reverse RF phase. Because B=∇×AL=0 for a pure longitudinal wave, a metal loop has no classical induction to work with. Zimmerman QEX 2011; J. Appl. Phys. 114, 044907 (2013); plasma responsivity cited ≈ 4.2×10⁵ A per Wb/m (2011 §5) or 1.86–2.64×10⁵ m/H (CEM-R-46 modeled). Bifilar pancake (Hively) The coil is geometrically matched to irrotational (gradient-driven) fields. Adjacent turns carry opposing current → net B≈0 and near-zero inductance. What remains is a gradient response: EL or −∂AL/∂t drives a coherent irrotational current to the terminals. JL ≈ σ EL EL = −∇Φ − ∂AL/∂t Do not parallel the two wires. Series-opposing (outer of A to inner of B) is the non-inductive connection. Face-on maximizes projected area (~78.5 cm² for a 10 cm palm coil in the SNR toys). US 9,306,527 B1; Hively & Land, J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 1956 012011 (2021). Zimmerman 2011 hardware — 1296 MHz circular waveguide First-class amateur-radio source (scan in the Library): Robert K. Zimmerman, NP4B / VE3RKZ, “Transmission and Reception of Longitudinally-Polarized Momentum Waves,” QEX July/August 2011, p. 31+. TEM vs vector-potential comparison and a 1296 MHz TM01 transmitter: Item As published / scanned Band 1296 MHz (23 cm amateur calling frequency) Waveguide 7-inch galvanized stovepipe, TM01 Cutoff λcut ≈ 23.23 cm Guide length 69 cm guide + 69 cm longitudinal probe Choke 5.8 cm choke collar Feed Type N + 3 dB pad Detector U-shaped fluorescent plasma tube TEM vs VP (author’s table) Both Maxwell, both speed c, both ~1/R amplitude; VP called longitudinal, momentum-carrying, not seen by ordinary metal antennas This is the natural N–Z-style transmitter to sit alongside the Hively RG-405 stub + skirt in the 1.3 GHz lab. It is still an experimental interpretation: a TM01 launcher plus a plasma detector does not, by itself, prove a new free-space channel. Papers, patents, reports Patent numbers are exact. Use Google Patents; do not rely on this page as legal text. Citation What it is Link US 8,165,531 B2 (2012). Nikolova, N.K. & Zimmerman, R.K. Jr. Electromagnetic wave-potential communication system and method. Assigned to McMaster University. Vector-potential / momentum-wave communications patent. Parabolic + longitudinal dipole embodiments. Google Patents US8165531B2 US 9,306,527 B1 (2016). Hively, L.M. Systems, apparatuses, and methods for generating and/or utilizing scalar-longitudinal waves. SLW patent: irrotational current, monopole + skirt, bifilar. Eq. 15 for Prad. Google Patents US9306527B1 Zimmerman, R.K. (2011). “Transmission and Reception of Longitudinally-Polarized Momentum Waves.” QEX Jul/Aug 2011, pp. 31–35. 1296 MHz TM01 stovepipe + plasma Rx. Local scan in Library. PDF (scan) Nikolova, N.K. & Zimmerman, R.K. (Nov 2007). Detection of the Time-dependent Electromagnetic Potential at 1.3 GHz. McMaster CEM-R-46. 1.3 GHz plasma detection of time-dependent 4-potential. McMaster report CEM-R-46 Zimmerman, R.K. (2013). J. Appl. Phys. 114, 044907. Plasma reception of longitudinal A. JAP 114, 044907 Hively, L.M. & Loebl, A.S. (2019). “Classical and extended electrodynamics.” Physics Essays 32(1), 112–126. EED exposition; copper-penetration discussion. Physics Essays 32(1) Hively, L.M. (2020). IARD 2020 presentation / paper. ~8 GHz monopole + skirt, copper Faraday tests, 1/r², isotropic claim. IARD 2020 PDF Hively, L.M. & Land, M. (2021). “Extended electrodynamics and SHP theory.” J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 1956 012011. EED + patent hardware language used in the SNR toys. JPCS 1956 012011 Alexander, D.S. (Apr 2005). NASA/CR-2005-213749. Advanced Energetics for Aeronautical Applications, Vol. II. Contractor survey (Steinmetz, Tesla vs Hertz, Valone, Puthoff US 5,845,220, Meyl). Institutional map, not NASA endorsement of over-unity. PDF Meyl, K. Scalar-wave lectures / “Scalar Waves: Theory and Experiments” (2001, 2004). Potential-vortex program. See also Bruhn, J. Scientific Exploration 15(2). INDEL / JSE Adjacent literature (AHE phonons, bagel-coil anecdote, laser-plasma vortices, company newsletter) lives on the Library page with explicit genre labels. Those items are not SLW hardware manuals. Related model sketch: C-field interaction with nuclei — educational coupling proposal (EED × nuclear sensors); not a LENR or decay-rate claim on this bench.

text: Exp B sphere SLW/SW claims require a Tekbox H-probe B-null near the RX ball (Hively). Rods optional for that null. Detail: kit.html#tekbox. Educational briefing · Europhys. Lett. 59, 514 (2002) · not settled physics Monstein & Wesley 2002: brass-rod polarizer for a claimed longitudinal E New: VNA guide for Steve: what to measure on the 433.59 MHz balls and rod cube with a VNA (M&W themselves did not use one). C. Monstein and J.P. Wesley reported a 433.59 MHz ball-antenna experiment they titled “Observation of scalar longitudinal electrodynamic waves.” This page is a study aid: what they built, the formulas in the paper, how later authors read it, and how it does and does not connect to Hively Faraday-cage SLW work, Nikolova–Zimmerman A(r), Meyl, and Puthoff polarizable-vacuum notes. Experiment B — no balun of any type. Coax into the ball, outer conductor as shield (MW Fig. 1 / Amphenol 901-9875). Not a sleeve, not a skirt, not a bazooka. Experiment A’s first article is now a ¾″ sphere too (setup.html#sphere-a); keep RF feeds electrically separate. Optional A sleeve/bifilar control still on setup.html#sleeve. Do not merge this page with the 1296 mesh-tent protocol. Paper in the Library. Author-hosted PDF (filename typo “electroydnamic”): jamespaulwesley.org copy · hub mirror papers/…. Licensed 23 cm (1296 MHz) or 13 cm (2.45 GHz ISM / ham segments) only if you replicate. No magnetron protocol. What they built Frequency. 433.59 MHz. λ = c/f ≈ 0.692 m. λ/2 = 34.6 cm (the rod length they quote). Source / detector. Identical aluminium ball antennas, 6 cm diameter, coax fed to the inside of the sphere (outer conductor as shield). Heights: source 4.0 m above ground, receiver 4.4 m. Polarizer-analyzer. Cubic array of nine brass λ/2 rods on a rotatable mount (hand or turntable). Absorb when rods are parallel to the claimed propagation direction; transmit when perpendicular. Two crossed arrays were proposed as a TEM filter. Range. Signal vs distance, including two interference minima they attribute to an Earth image source. They argue only a wave (not a near-zone quasi-static field) can show that plus ~1/r². Redrawn in words: TX ball → (optional rod cube at angle φ) → RX ball, both balls well above a ground plane. That is a polarizer test for the direction of E, not a Faraday-cage skin-depth test and not a bifilar pancake. Formulas as written in the 2002 letter Gaussian units in the original. They start from a retarded scalar potential (their eq. 1; typesetting of the d’Alembertian is as printed): ∇²Φ − (1/c²) ∂²Φ/∂t² = −4πρ (1) ρ = q δ(r − r′) sin(ωt) (3) Φ = q sin(kr − ωt) / r (4) E = ∇Φ = [k q cos(kr − ωt)/r − q sin(kr − ωt)/r²] ê_r (5) ⟨S⟩_t = (k ω q / (2 r²)) ê_r (6) Ohmic loss in a rod of conductivity σ and cross-section A, only the component E₀ cos φ along the wire (φ = angle between rods and the TX–RX line): δP = −σ A E₀² cos²(φ) δL (7) T = exp[ −κ cos²(φ) ] (9) κ_fit = 4.4 (their fig. 3 best fit; κ ∝ L) Ground-image sketch: observed field as superposition of amplitude A from the source at height y and B from an image at y′ (they place the reflecting surface λ/2 = 34.6 cm below the actual earth). Energy ~1/r² with interference minima. We do not reproduce their fitted A, B tables; read eqs. (12)–(15) in the letter. CED reading: a spherically fed ball is not a proof that ∇·A = 0 forbids TEM. Feed cables, the ground, and the rod array all break spherical symmetry. Bray & Britton (EPL 2004) and Rębilas (EPL 2008) press that point. This hub lists MW’s equations so you can see what they claimed, not so you treat them as Maxwell. Precision TX–RX distance control (Experiment B) Hively wants precision distance control for TX–RX separation on this bench too. Polarizer rods are Experiment B only (not used on the 1296 MHz Exp A sphere/mesh bench). Near-field floors @ 433.59 MHz (λ ≈ 0.692 m): reactive near field ≈ λ/(2π) ≈ 110 mm (4.3″). Conservative logged start: ≳ 2–3 λ ≈ 1.4–2.1 m (about 4.5–7 ft); MW-style outdoor/garage baselines are meters. Do not park RX (or the ~0.35 m rod cube) inside ~λ/(2π) of either ball. Baseline: longer than Exp A — garage / driveway / outdoors. Fixed TX ball stand; movable RX; optional rod cube on its own non-metallic stand between them (log cube position separately). Readout: surveyor's tape or marked floor tape + laser rangefinder. Log r ball-to-ball (and cube station if used). Hardware: non-metallic track or fiducial marks; keep steel rails and long coax out of the aperture. Support/rotator for rods: shop-drawing.html#sheet-support. Exp A bench ranging (shorter rail): setup.html#ranging-a · combined sheet: shop-drawing.html#sheet-ranging. Later seawater: Tomilin 2021 is a Tesla–sphere HF marine channel, not this land rod polarizer. Gap list (Nanuk land ≠ immersed hulls): kit.html#tomilin-gaps · library.html#tomilin-2021. Rods stay Exp B land-only unless a separate boat control is logged. Why the rods are λ/2, not λ/4 Steve Morris asked a fair novice question: aren’t antennas supposed to be a quarter-wavelength? These brass (and optional W1) rods are not driven antennas. The two aluminium balls are the TX and RX. The nine rods are a parasitic polarizer-analyzer: they absorb when the electric field has a component along the wire. A thin isolated wire is a resonant half-wave dipole when L ≈ λ/2. Induced current (and ohmic loss) peaks there. Monstein & Wesley 2002 cut the rods to λ/2 so the cube is a resonant absorber for E∥k. Numbers at 433.59 MHz: λ = c/f = 299792458 / 433.59e6 ≈ 0.691 m (69.1 cm) λ/2 ≈ 34.6 cm (MW’s rod length) λ/4 ≈ 17.3 cm λ/4 is the classic monopole over a ground plane (a driven antenna: one λ/4 arm plus its image). The polarizer has no ground plane and is not fed, so λ/2 — two λ/4 arms, a full dipole — is the right resonant length. Steve’s λ/4 instinct is correct for a stub/monopole, wrong for these floating rods. MW eq. (7) δP = −σ A E₀² cos²φ δL and (9) T = exp[−κ cos²φ] with κ ∝ L and κ_fit = 4.4 is the brass λ/2 fit. Off-resonance, that DC-ohmic picture is incomplete: current has nodes, so a longer rod is not automatically a stronger polarizer. If they do not cut the 3 ft (91.4 cm ≈ 1.32 λ) store-bought sticks Negatives. Off-resonance, so a shallower U / weaker T(φ) contrast. The 3×3 cube becomes ~0.9 m on a side instead of ~0.35 m — hard to rotate, more diffraction. It is not a 2002 replication. Hively’s hysteresis swap also specified the same 34.6 cm geometry. Positives. No cutting; cheaper first look. Some E∥ vs E⊥ contrast can still appear (anisotropic loss). MW’s κ∝L formula would naively predict more attenuation — do not treat that as a prediction at 1.32 λ. Recommendation. Cut brass (and W1) to 34.6 cm for the replication. Log uncut only as a named deviation. Rotation curve (the U) If T = exp[−κ cos² φ] and you rotate the cube through 360°, transmission is high near φ = 90° / 270° (rods across the path) and low near φ = 0° / 180° (rods along the path). That is a U (two dips per full turn). MW’s κ = 4.4 is an ohmic-brass fit, not a magnetic-hysteresis fit. This is an educational JS canvas, not settled physics and not a Wolfram Cloud player. They leave the mechanism unidentified. Hively’s scientific distinction (2026, personal communication) Paraphrase only. Not a quotation. Not an endorsement that the 2002 result is settled. Monstein–Wesley showed an electric field along the direction of propagation using brass rods as a polarizer. That is a statement about E∥k, not about a dynamical scalar C. They did not detect Hively’s scalar field (the EED C = ∇·A + c⁻² ∂Φ/∂t that appears with the SLW in US 9,306,527). Suggested follow-on (unpublished method; attribute: L.M. The “sleeve balun, not skirt” note from that era belongs to the 1.3 GHz monopole/cage (Experiment A, setup.html#sleeve), not to this 433.59 MHz ball feed — Experiment B has no balun. Hively US 9,306,527 Eq. 15 Partial P_rad = I_pk² Z₀ / (4π), Faraday-cage SLW, bifilar + sleeve-stub (Experiment A; patent Fig. 2A skirt is historical). Different antenna and a claimed C field MW did not measure. Nikolova–Zimmerman A(r) Loose A_m = μ₀ I / (2π k₀ r) (CEM-R-46 / hub fields page). Vector potential along a TM₀₁ / plasma-detector story, not brass-rod polarizer. Meyl potential vortices Vocabulary only Third language on this hub. Do not import over-unity or superluminal claims into a Monstein budget. Puthoff 2005 PV / Levi-Civita Not the same experiment Gen. Rel. Grav. 37, 483 (2005) is polarizable-vacuum GR (Levi-Civita), not a NASA SEW / underwater TM paper. Shield / dense-media claims sit in US 5,845,220 and later EarthTech patents — different lineage from MW rods. Reed & Hively 2020 Yes, cites MW Open-access Symmetry 12, 2110 (2020) is the paper that actually cites Monstein. Physics Essays 2019 remains closed-access; use the OA 2020 letter when you need a public Hively citation. Same lab language as fields: CED = TEM. SLW / longitudinal Φ-waves = disputed. Quote mesh dB or polarizer T(φ), not 25,000 dB copper myths, when you go to 1.3 GHz tents. Parts for this bench (not the pancake cage) This list is for the Monstein–Wesley 433.59 MHz ball + rod polarizer (and the 2026 personal-communication hysteresis-rod swap). It is not the 1296 MHz RadioScreen pancake protocol on setup.html. Different bench. Do not kit RadioScreen mesh, Pelican 1200, a Cricut mat, or the bifilar pancake here. 433.59 MHz is in the US 70 cm amateur band (λ ≈ 69.2 cm; λ/2 = 34.6 cm). Technician-class operators may use it under Part 97 with a valid license, identification, and band-edge rules. It is not the EU 433 MHz Part-15 / SRD ISM allocation when you transmit in the US. Educational only; SLW / longitudinal E is not settled physics. Shop pages (McMaster, K-Mac, Speedy Metals, Amidon, VXB, DigiKey) are often JavaScript-heavy — open the catalog in a full browser if a fetch looks empty. Aluminium spheres (need two) MW 2002 used 6 cm aluminium balls with coax into the sphere (outer conductor as shield). Butterworth’s reconstruction used ~3″ aluminium. Closest catalog hollow aluminium with a ¼″ hole already in the ball (fits an SMA bulkhead): Correspondence page: is the 2.50″ 3003 Aluminum hollow ball + 901-9875 an acceptable Fig. 1 substitute? (Experiment B only; photos and comparison table.) Catalog vs exact Fig. 1 shop-hours (prices ~Sep 2026): sphere.html#cost. K-Mac Plastics 3003 Aluminum hollow balls, catalog k-mac-plastics.com/balls/hollow-metal-balls.htm (JS-heavy). ¼″ hole is already there. 2.50″ (63.5 mm) KB-2016 3003 Aluminum hollow, $126.96 each; two (TX+RX) ≈ $253.92 before shipping — closest to MW 6 cm. 2.00″ KB-2014 ~$60 each — smaller, cheaper. 3.00″ KB-2015 ~$132 each — Butterworth-ish ~3″. Do not buy Meyl stainless 60 mm balls as the primary spheres. Last-resort cheap 60 mm stainless stair-cap only: Amazon uxcell 2-pack (B07R4735PQ) — wrong metal, gold coat, not a 50 Ω feed. Brass rods (need nine × 34.6 cm) — MW baseline polarizer Experiment B only. These rods are not part of Experiment A (1296 MHz ¾″ sphere / mesh tents). Printable shop drawing — cut & deburr Support block + rotator jig Ohmic E∥k polarizer. 1/8″ diameter is a convenient polarizer size; MW did not freeze a unique gauge. McMaster 360 brass round, 1/8″ dia, family 8953K101. Buy 3 ft (or 2 ft) sticks; nine × 34.6 cm. 36″ = 91.4 cm; 91.4 / 34.6 = 2.64, so two finished 34.6 cm rods per stick (leftover ~22 cm; do not splice). Four sticks yield only eight rods. Buy five 36″ sticks for nine rods (ten cuts, one spare). Cut to 34.6 cm. Alternate catalog: McMaster brass alloy 360 rods. High-hysteresis rods (need nine, same geometry) — optional second article Hively’s unpublished method (L.M. Hively, 2026, personal communication; not a MW figure; no private email is reproduced). Keep the same 3×3 cube and 34.6 cm length. Rotate 360° and look for a U-curve. Not mu-metal (low hysteresis). This hub does not claim the swap has been run. 1/8″ W1 water-hardening drill rod (same geometry as the brass λ/2 polarizer, nine × 34.6 cm): Speedy Metals 1/8 RD W-1 drill rod, $11.11 per 36″ stick. 36″ = 91.4 cm; 91.4 / 34.6 = 2.64, so two finished 34.6 cm rods per stick (leftover ~22 cm; do not splice). Four sticks yield only eight rods. Buy five 36″ sticks for nine rods (ten cuts, one spare). Five sticks ≈ $55.55 before cutting/shipping. Procurable high-carbon / high B–H-loop stand-in for Hively’s unpublished “high-magnetic-hysteresis rods,” not a claim it is his exact alloy. Cut to 34.6 cm. Ferrite is a second, lossier UHF option and is not sold in 34.6 cm sticks — do not claim ferrite ≡ Hively’s unspecified alloy. Amidon R61-050-400 0.5″×4″: amidoncorp.com/r61-050-400 12 mm × 200 mm 5-pack: VXB ferrite rods 12 mm × 200 mm — would need end-to-end stacking to approach 34.6 cm; say so in the log. Cables (TinySA Ultra SMA female → sphere) The TinySA Ultra RF port is SMA female, so the instrument end needs an SMA plug (male). Keep each jumper inside its Faraday enclosure; no jumper between TX and RX boxes (Hively scatter note: cabling outside the enclosures). Qty 2 (TX + RX). Verified DigiKey 12″ RG-316 50 Ω SMA: Amphenol 135111-01-12.00 (RA plug to SMA). Straight-plug twin is Amphenol 135101-01-12.00 (same family; search DigiKey if the right-angle 135111 is awkward). Better for the ball: Amphenol 135110-01-12.00 SMA straight plug to SMA bulkhead jack on RG-316 (mount the jack in the sphere’s ¼″ hole). Search DigiKey/Mouser for 135110-01-12.00 rather than a guessed product URL. Qty 2. The Ultra kit already includes two ~30 cm SMA cables; those can be used if they are SMA-M both ends — still add bulkhead jacks on the balls (see #bulkhead). SMA bulkhead (¼″ hole in each Al sphere) Feed geometry vs Fig. 1 (machined 10H7/3H7 cavity): see sphere.html. Full install notes: sphere.html#sma-install. Novice gender chain (keep SMA genders correct): the TinySA Ultra RF port is a hole (SMA-F). The jumper cable has a pin on each end (SMA-M/M). The bulkhead is the fitting through the ¼″ hole in the aluminium sphere; the outside of the bulkhead is also a hole so the cable pin screws on. Qty 2 (TX ball + RX ball). Not a Meyl part. This is the 433.59 MHz / 70 cm Technician ball feed, not the 1296 mesh-tent bench on setup.html. Qty 2 purchased 2 Sep 2026 (RF Parts) — Amphenol 901-9875, SMA jack/female, bulkhead, crimp for RG-316 / LMR-100A (cable group B), 50 Ω, $11.90 each: RF Parts 901-9875. Gold-plated brass body, BeCu gold center, PTFE. Prefer this SKU as the “coax into the interior” part (crimp RG-316, center soldered inside the sphere). Same SKU also listed at TestEquity if a spare is needed later. Thread: 1/4-36 UNEF (¼″-36 Unified Extra Fine). Jack–jack pass-through alternative (hole on both sides of the ball wall): Amphenol 901-9209-A SMA bulkhead F–F, ¼-36. Search DigiKey/Mouser for 901-9209-A rather than a guessed product URL. Then still SMA-M/M Ultra to the outside; inside the ball you either solder a short post to the inner contact or use a tiny SMA-M pigtail. 901-9875 remains the better interior-coax part. After mate: NanoRFE VNA6000-A S11 of each ball around 433.59 MHz; TDR jumpers — kit.html#vna6000. Rods are not a 2-port VNA DUT. Machine-shop / install — is ¼″ proper for tapping? Printable shop drawing (Exp B) No. The existing ¼″ (0.250″) hole is not a tap drill for 1/4-36 UNEF — it is essentially the thread major diameter, so there is little/no material left to cut threads. Do not recommend tapping that hole as the primary plan. Thin hollow-ball walls usually cannot take a reliable tapped thread without a boss or other thickening. Preferred: clearance + locknut/washer. Recommended clearance / panel hole 6.5 mm (≈ 0.256″) (window ~6.3–6.6 mm). If the bulkhead will not slide in the stock ¼″ hole, ream carefully to 6.5 mm / letter F (≈ 0.257″). Deburr for O-ring/flange seating. Mate 901-9875: feed coax into the interior; bond outer conductor / bulkhead body to the ball shell (MW outer-as-shield). Center to a short post or inner contact. No balun. If the nut will not fit: exterior flange/solder fillet + conductive bond; or solder/weld a boss then tap 1/4-36 UNEF 2B into the boss only (≥2–3 full pitches); tap drill #3 (0.2130″) usual, or #2 (0.2210″) sometimes in Al — confirm shop chart + datasheet. Temporary access for nutting is another option. PTFE or nylon insulating washers only if you intentionally do not want the shield bonded to the whole shell (default MW framing bonds outer as shield). Non-metallic rotator for the 3×3 cube: HDPE/acrylic preferred (styrofoam = mock-up only). Printable support + turntable / optional motor sheet: shop-drawing.html#sheet-support. HDPE/acrylic plate stock on setup.html#shop is shared hardware, not the same bench. Parallel thread facts for Experiment A’s ¾″ ball: setup.html#sma-shop-a. Will a Meyl ball-antenna kit do Hively’s protocol? No as a kit. Partial only if you scavenge the two spheres and rebuild everything else at UHF. Do not treat Meyl potential-vortex / over-unity language as Hively’s C field. What meyl.eu actually sells (Demo / Experimental kits): Tesla pancake coils with two spherical electrodes on plastic columns, a low-impedance waveform generator, cables, LEDs, optional frequency counter. Demo generator about 4–8 MHz; Experimental historically ~0.2–14 MHz analog or DDS to ~8–10 MHz after 2014. Coil types quoted ~3.5 / 7 / 14 MHz. Typical bench distance in the manual is tens of centimetres with a ground strap between pancake outer turns. That is HF Tesla-coil-plus-ball, not a 433 MHz ball feed and not a 23 cm lab. Monstein–Wesley 2002 Hively follow-on (2026, pers. comm.) Meyl kit Frequency 433.59 MHz (λ ≈ 69 cm) 1.296 GHz or 2.45 GHz kHz–low MHz (λ tens of metres) TX/RX 6 cm aluminium balls, coax into the sphere, no balun Same 433.59 MHz balls, still no balun; TX in one Faraday enclosure, RX in another. Sleeve-stub is Experiment A, not this feed. Pancake coil + ball; open bench, LED load Polarizer Nine λ/2 brass rods (34.6 cm), rotate for T(φ) Same geometry, then high-hysteresis rods, 360° U-curve None Metrology Distance + image interference Time-stamp TX droop, Signal Hound-class RX, positioner; no cables outside the FEs Resonance vs ball size / spacing Buy the kit if you want to play Meyl’s HF pancake demonstrations. Do not buy it as a substitute for nine λ/2 rods, a rotator, two Faraday boxes, or a licensed 1296 / 2.45 GHz source. Two metal spheres are cheap without the suitcase. λ/2 at 1296 MHz is 11.6 cm; at 2.45 GHz 6.1 cm — scale the rods, not a 7 MHz pancake. If someone replicates under Part 97 Keep the MW ball feed: coax into the sphere, outer as shield, no balun. Identify; milliwatts; 70 cm Technician-legal. If you ever scale the polarizer rods to 1296 or 2.45 GHz that is still this geometry (balls + rods), not a sleeve-stub. The 1296 Faraday-cage sleeve lives on setup.html#sleeve. Two Faraday enclosures: TX stack in one, RX (Signal Hound class or TinySA Ultra 406) in the other. No cables out on a “sealed” run. Time-stamp TX power, RX, and rotator angle on one clock. Brass-rod baseline: nine λ/2 rods, 360° rotation, log T(φ). Optional second article: high-hysteresis rods, same geometry, look for a U. That second article is Hively’s unpublished suggestion, not a MW figure. Hively’s suggested follow-on stays on this bench (Experiment B): two Faraday enclosures + 433.59 MHz balls with no balun + rod cube — not the pancake / RadioScreen shopping list and not a sleeve-build. The 1296 MHz sphere / mesh-tent bench (¾″ KB-1820 first article; bifilar optional) is a different bench: setup.html#sphere-a. DOI: Monstein & Wesley, EPL 59, 514 (2002). This page © 2026 Dan Britton, educational use. Scalar / longitudinal claims are not IEEE-standard antenna theory.

Checking that the tip really is at the center
