description: Machine-shop drill patterns for acrylic jigs holding the Monstein & Wesley 3×3 λ/2 rod polarizer-analyzer at 433.59 MHz, scaled to 1296 MHz and 2.45 GHz. FACT / HYPOTHESIS / IDEA labels.
text: Analysis page · shop drawings · Experiment B (M&W) + Experiment A and 2.45 GHz extensions Acrylic Rod-Holding Jigs for the Monstein & Wesley Polarizer-Analyzer Three machine-shop drill patterns (one per frequency) for the plastic plates that hold nine parallel λ/2 rods in a 3 × 3 grid. The rods pass through one plate at mid-length, as in the M&W photo. You need two identical plates per frequency: one for the horizontal-rod array (turns on a turntable) and one for the vertical-rod array (fixed). DRAFT, for Dan's review. These drawings have not been built or checked in a shop yet, and nothing has been ordered. Before drilling the real plates, try the reamer on a test coupon. Educational only. Mainstream electrodynamics treats free-space radio waves as transverse. The M&W longitudinal-wave claim is disputed (Bray & Britton 2004; Rębilas 2008). Butterworth et al. (2013) rebuilt the setup and did not see the polarizer null. This page covers mechanical geometry only. FACT stated in a cited paper, or plain arithmetic HYPOTHESIS an interpretation or extension, not in the papers IDEA our design choice; change it if you like 1 · Drawings Experiment B · 433.59 MHz Jig_ExpB_433MHz.pdf · 3 letter sheets (drill pattern · section + hole detail + tables · cut list + assembly + notes) Experiment A · 1296 MHz Jig_ExpA_1296MHz.pdf · 3 letter sheets (drill pattern · section + hole detail + tables · cut list + assembly + notes) 2.45 GHz band Jig_2450MHz.pdf · 3 letter sheets (drill pattern · section + hole detail + tables · cut list + assembly + notes) Sheet 1 for Exp A and 2.45 GHz is full size (1:1 on US Letter). Print it at 100 % and check the scale bar. Sheet 1 for Exp B is drawn at 1:4, because a 15″ plate does not fit on Letter. Its full-size coordinates are in the table. Numbers: numbers.json. 2 · Geometry check Item Request M&W 2002 (EPL 59(4) 514) Butterworth et al. 2013 (446 MHz) Used here Rods 9, half-wave FACT "cubic array of 9 wires of length λ/2 (34.6 cm)", brass (p. 516, Fig. 2) FACT "nine wires in 3 × 3 arrays, a half-wavelength long" 9 × λ/2 (matches) Spacing λ/4 Not stated FACT "a quarter-wave apart" λ/4, sourced from Butterworth, not M&W Arrays one horizontal, one vertical, rotatable FACT Fig. 2 is a single rotatable 3×3, "turned by hand or … disc record player". Text: "Two such arrays with wires perpendicular to the direction of propagation and to each other serve as a filter" FACT "one horizontal and one vertical. The horizontal polarizer can be rotated." 2 arrays per frequency; H rotates, V fixed Mounting not given FACT (photo) horizontal rods through one vertical wooden board at about mid-length not described one plate at rod mid-length Ball antenna 6 cm FACT "ball antenna, 6 cm diameter" (abstract, Fig. 1) FACT solid 3″ (76 mm) Al balls; M&W described as r = 30 mm not part of the jig (hub B ball is KB-2016, 2.50″) Rod dia, board size, array position not given Not stated Not stated IDEA 1/8″ rods; plate sizes below HYPOTHESIS "Cubic": a 3 × 3 grid at λ/4 pitch is λ/2 across, the same as the rod length, so the nine rods fill a λ/2 cube. This is our reading of the word and supports Butterworth's λ/4. Discrepancy flagged: the request's "spaced λ/4" and "one horizontal, one vertical" wording comes from Butterworth's reconstruction, not from M&W. M&W's measured curve (Fig. 3) used one rotating array. 3 · Frequencies and sources FACT Experiment B = 433.59 MHz: the M&W frequency (abstract, p. 515). Also on hub monstein.html and setup.html, Dipole Detector DD-433, and the rod-fixtures rev A drawings. Experiment A = 1296.000 MHz: hub setup.html ("1296.000 MHz", lines 78/102), shop-drawing.html Sheet A, sleeve-balun.html, DD-1296 (dipole_numbers.json), and the Hively 1.3 GHz protocol ("1296.000 MHz" is the preferred lab carrier). 1294.5 MHz is not on the hub or in the ledger (checked hub origin/main 8e53b6a). The only 1294.5 on the box is in hively-1.3ghz-faraday-lab-protocol.md line 107: "do not put a CW carrier on FM simplex 1294.5". The jig uses 1296.000. HYPOTHESIS scaling to Exp A is Dan's extension. The hub (shop-drawing.html:506, monstein.html) still says polarizer rods are Exp B only. 2.45 GHz = 2450.0 MHz: DD-2450 build sheet, rod-fixtures Future_2450MHz, and the oven magnetron nominal. HYPOTHESIS scaling. Use the jig outside the oven only. Never put rods inside a running microwave oven. 4 · Numbers per frequency Experiment B · 433.59 MHz Experiment A · 1296 MHz 2.45 GHz band Frequency 433.59 MHz FACT 1296.000 MHz HYPOTHESIS 2450.0 MHz HYPOTHESIS λ = c/f 691.42 mm 231.32 mm 122.36 mm Rod length (λ/2, free space) 346.00 ± 1.0 mm (13.622″) · M&W 34.6 cm 115.66 ± 0.3 mm (4.554″) 61.18 ± 0.2 mm (2.409″) Pitch (λ/4) 172.85 mm (6.8053″) 57.83 mm (2.2768″) 30.59 mm (1.2044″) Rod diameter 1/8″ = 3.175 mm (brass, then W1) 1/8″ = 3.175 mm (brass, then W1) 1/8″ = 3.175 mm (brass, then W1) Hole Ø3.175 mm ream thru, +0.013/−0 mm (size to measured rod) Ø3.175 mm ream thru, +0.013/−0 mm (size to measured rod) Ø3.175 mm ream thru, +0.013/−0 mm (size to measured rod) Hole position tol. ±0.25 mm (±0.010″) ±0.13 mm (±0.005″) ±0.13 mm (±0.005″) Rod plate (qty 2) 15.00″ sq × 0.5″ cast acrylic (381.0 mm, t = 12.70 mm) 6.00″ sq × 0.5″ cast acrylic (152.4 mm, t = 12.70 mm) 4.00″ sq × 0.25″ cast acrylic (101.6 mm, t = 6.35 mm) Edge margin (hole centre) 17.65 mm (5.6× rod dia) 18.37 mm (5.8× rod dia) 20.21 mm (6.4× rod dia) Rod protrusion each side 166.65 mm 51.48 mm 27.41 mm Plate t / rod L 0.037 0.110 0.104 V-array leg height 7.625″ (194 mm) 3.125″ (79 mm) 2.125″ (54 mm) Acrylic area (net / +20 %) 912.8 / 1095.3 in² 154.5 / 185.4 in² 74.0 / 88.8 in² Acrylic mass 8.90 kg 1.51 kg 0.36 kg Buy 1 × 24×48″ × ½″ 1 × 12×24″ × ½″ 1 × 12×12″ × ¼″ Drawing scale (sheet 1) 1:4 + full-size table 1:1 (template) 1:1 (template) The only electrical formula is λ = c/f with c = 299 792 458 m/s. Rod length is the free-space λ/2, which is M&W's own definition: 34.6 cm at 433.59 MHz, compared with 345.71 mm computed; the hub cuts 346 ± 1 mm. These are polarizer rods, not the resonance-shortened Dipole Detector elements. Hole grid: 3 × 3 at λ/4, centred on the plate. Experiment B · 433.59 MHz: hole coordinates (mm) Hole X from corner O Y from corner O X from centre C Y from centre C H1 17.65 17.65 -172.85 -172.85 H2 190.50 17.65 +0.00 -172.85 H3 363.35 17.65 +172.85 -172.85 H4 17.65 190.50 -172.85 +0.00 H5 190.50 190.50 +0.00 +0.00 H6 363.35 190.50 +172.85 +0.00 H7 17.65 363.35 -172.85 +172.85 H8 190.50 363.35 +0.00 +172.85 H9 363.35 363.35 +172.85 +172.85 Experiment A · 1296 MHz: hole coordinates (mm) Hole X from corner O Y from corner O X from centre C Y from centre C H1 18.37 18.37 -57.83 -57.83 H2 76.20 18.37 +0.00 -57.83 H3 134.03 18.37 +57.83 -57.83 H4 18.37 76.20 -57.83 +0.00 H5 76.20 76.20 +0.00 +0.00 H6 134.03 76.20 +57.83 +0.00 H7 18.37 134.03 -57.83 +57.83 H8 76.20 134.03 +0.00 +57.83 H9 134.03 134.03 +57.83 +57.83 2.45 GHz band: hole coordinates (mm) Hole X from corner O Y from corner O X from centre C Y from centre C H1 20.21 20.21 -30.59 -30.59 H2 50.80 20.21 +0.00 -30.59 H3 81.39 20.21 +30.59 -30.59 H4 20.21 50.80 -30.59 +0.00 H5 50.80 50.80 +0.00 +0.00 H6 81.39 50.80 +30.59 +0.00 H7 20.21 81.39 -30.59 +30.59 H8 50.80 81.39 +0.00 +30.59 H9 81.39 81.39 +30.59 +30.59 5 · Hole fit in acrylic Spec on the drawings IDEA: ream to the measured rod diameter, nominal 0.1250″ (3.175 mm), with tolerance +0.0005/−0.0000″ (+0.013/−0 mm). That gives a snug (transition) fit, not a press fit. The rods are held by silicone O-rings (AS568-005) on both faces. Rods must be swappable, since Hively's plan is brass first and then W1 in the same geometry, and they must stay electrically floating. Drilling: pilot Ø3.0 mm (or #32), peck with water mist, use a dubbed zero-rake bit and a sacrificial backer, then ream. Chamfer 0.4 × 45° on both faces. Anneal before solvent cementing. Why not the requested 0.05–0.10 mm undersize? Acrylic makers advise against press fits and against high local stress: "design loads should not exceed 750 psi" for continuous loading (American Plastics Corp. acrylic data); Plaskolite and Perspex guides say to oversize holes and minimise stress. We estimated the hoop stress at the bore for a rigid rod in a thick plate as σ ≈ E·(δ/D)/(1+ν), with E ≈ 3.1 GPa and ν ≈ 0.37 ASSUMPTION: Interference (diametral) mm hoop strain hoop stress psi ÷ 750 psi requested 0.05 mm under 0.0500 1.57 % 5,168 6.9× requested 0.10 mm under 0.1000 3.15 % 10,337 13.8× HDPE fixture #31 (0.120 in) 0.127 mm under 0.1270 4.00 % 13,128 17.5× light press 0.013 mm (0.0005 in) 0.0127 0.40 % 1,313 1.8× 0.0075 mm (0.0003 in) 0.0076 0.24 % 788 1.1× 750 psi continuous corresponds to only about 7.3 µm of interference, which a drilled hole cannot reliably hold. So the drawings specify a snug fit plus O-rings. The #31 (0.120″) light press used on the earlier HDPE fixtures works in HDPE because it is ductile. It must not be carried over to acrylic. Fallback if Dan wants a press fit: measured rod diameter minus 0.0005″ (about 1,300 psi), on cast acrylic only, annealed, and tested on the coupon first. 6 · Design choices FACT M&W Fig. 2 shows rods passing through one board at mid-length. IDEA We follow that: one plate per array, rods centred with equal protrusion. IDEA Not a solid block. The hub's 380 × 380 × 50–75 mm block would weigh about 9–13 kg in acrylic and put plastic over 14–22 % of each rod. Not two end plates either: that would put plastic at the rod tips and departs from the photo. Plate thickness: ½″ for Exp B (t/L 0.037) and Exp A (0.110), ¼″ for 2.45 GHz (0.104). IDEA H array: the rod plate is cemented into a half-depth dado in a square base, which sits on a turntable, so rotating it changes φ. V array: the rod plate is horizontal, cemented between two legs. Use solvent cement (Weld-On 16/4) only. No metal fasteners near the rods. IDEA 1/8″ rods for all three frequencies, for practical and structural reasons: that is the stock on hand or ordered (brass, and W1 drill rod), and one reamer serves every plate. The half-rod self-weight sag is only 0.13 mm for brass at 433 MHz. 1/16″ would bend in handling. The rod material enters M&W's model only through σ (eq. 7). IDEA Keep steel (turntable bearing, screws) at least λ/(2π) from the nearest rod: 110 / 37 / 20 mm. This is by analogy with the hub's "keep ≳ λ/(2π) from either ball". Add a wood or plastic riser if needed. Change from earlier work: the rod-fixtures rev A drawings (2026-09-26) were HDPE (McMaster 9785T833 6×6×¾ ×6 and 8612N17 15×15×¾ ×3, already delivered). This request specifies acrylic, and the drawings follow it. Rod lengths and pitches match rev A. 7 · Rod ringing and settle time ESTIMATE Each rod is held at mid-length in one acrylic plate, so mechanically it behaves as two cantilevers, one on each side of the plate. Every 10° turntable step bumps the rods, and they ring at their lowest bending mode until the motion dies away. A rod that is still swinging moves slightly in the field, which can wobble an S21 or TinySA reading taken too soon after the step. These are mechanical frequencies (Hz to kHz). They do not shift the 433.59 MHz to 2.45 GHz carrier; they can only make the reading wobble while the rods move. Lowest bending mode (estimate) Experiment B · 433.59 MHz 346.00 mm rod Experiment A · 1296 MHz 115.66 mm rod 2.45 GHz band 61.18 mm rod Cantilever length L (half rod to protrusion) 173.00 to 166.65 mm 57.83 to 51.48 mm 30.59 to 27.41 mm Brass about 51 to 55 Hz about 455 to 575 Hz about 1.6 to 2.0 kHz W1 tool steel about 76 to 82 Hz about 0.68 to 0.86 kHz about 2.4 to 3.0 kHz Ring-down time constant τ at Q ≈ 100 (brass / W1) about 0.6 / 0.4 s about 0.07 / 0.05 s about 0.02 / 0.01 s Time to ring down to about 5 % (3τ), brass about 2 s about 0.2 s about 0.06 s How the numbers were made ASSUMPTION: Euler-Bernoulli cantilever, first mode, f1 = (1.875² / 2π) · (d/4) · √(E/ρ) / L², with rod diameter d = 1/8″ = 3.175 mm. Brass E ≈ 100 GPa, ρ ≈ 8500 kg/m³; W1 tool steel E ≈ 207 GPa, ρ ≈ 7850 kg/m³ (typical handbook values; annealing barely changes E). L runs from the half rod length (clamp at the rod centre, lower frequency) to the protrusion beyond each plate face from section 4 (rigid clamp at the face, higher frequency). The snug fit and O-rings of section 5 are softer than a rigid clamp, so the real frequency should sit in or a little below this range. Q ≈ 100 is assumed, not measured; the O-rings add damping, so the real Q is probably lower and the ringing dies faster. τ = Q / (π f1). The second bending mode is about 6.3 times higher and dies out sooner. Procedure IDEA: After each 10° step, take your hands off the turntable and wait a settle time before reading. 3 s is a safe default on every band (the longest brass rods need about 2 s). Or watch the live trace (VNA S21 at the carrier, or a TinySA in zero span) and read once it is flat. Log the settle time in the settle_s column of the CSV template. Optional check, once per band and material: at one angle, read at about 0.5 s and again at 3 s after a step. If the two differ by more than the scatter of repeated readings, lengthen the settle time. If a motor or record-player drive turns the array (M&W Fig. 2 mentions one), stop it before each reading. A fixture that keeps turning keeps the rods excited. The bending shape (fixed at the plate, largest swing at the tip) can be visualised with Bob Greenyer's Standing Wave Project, a free browser tool for elastic and acoustic modes (no login), also used on the Experiment H page. Thanks to Bob Greenyer. To be clear about its limits here: the frequencies above come from the hand formula, not from the tool. A 3.2 mm rod up to 346 mm long is about 100 times longer than it is thick, and the tool's in-browser FEM grid (about 40 × 40 × 40 cells) cannot resolve that, so for these rods it shows the mode shape only, not a trustworthy frequency. 8 · Material and purchase Per frequency: 2 rod plates, 1 H base, 2 V legs and 1 fit-test coupon (3×3″). Standard cast-acrylic sheets come in 12×12, 12×24, 24×24, 24×48 and 48×96″, in ⅛, ¼, ⅜, ½, ¾ and 1″ thicknesses. Nesting was checked with a guillotine shelf-pack and ⅛″ kerf. Jig net in² +20 % in² Thickness Buy Exp B 433.59 MHz 912.75 1095.3 ½″ 1 × 24×48″ (1152 in²) Exp A 1296 MHz 154.5 185.4 ½″ 1 × 12×24″ (288 in²) 2.45 GHz 74.0 88.8 ¼″ 1 × 12×12″ (144 in²) Verdict: there is no acrylic stock on record. The only plastic on record is the HDPE bought for rev A. hub setup.html lists Amazon 6×6×⅛″ acrylic links, but those are shopping suggestions, not receipts, and ⅛″ is too thin for these plates anyway. Buy 3 pieces of cast acrylic (not extruded): ½″ 24×48, ½″ 12×24 and ¼″ 12×12. You can also order the 15 parts cut to size, which saves shop sawing. Prices have not been checked. Alternative: the HDPE Dan already owns fits the rev A plates (15×15 and 6×6), if he prefers not to buy acrylic. 9 · Open items WL check owed: src/RodJigCheck.wl is written but has not been run. There is no wolframscript on the box and the Wolfram Cloud key is unset. Numbers were computed in Python (src/jig_numbers.py). Measure the actual rod diameters (brass and W1) before picking the reamer. Brass rod tolerance is looser than drill rod. Stand height (centre rod H5 on the TX–RX axis) depends on the ball mounts, which are still open. Sheet prices are not verified, and the O-ring part number should be checked against the measured rod. Hub conflict remains: shop-drawing.html says "Rods / polarizer: None (Exp B only)", while Dan now wants Exp A and 2.45 GHz arrays. 10 · Sources C. Monstein & J. P. Wesley, "Observation of scalar longitudinal electrodynamic waves", Europhys. Lett. 59(4) 514–520 (2002), doi:10.1209/epl/i2002-00136-9. Cited: p. 516 text, Fig. 2 photo/caption, Fig. 1, eq. (7). E. J. Butterworth, C. B. Allison, D. Cavazos & F. M. Mullen, "Longitudinal Electromagnetic Waves? The Monstein–Wesley Experiment Reconstructed", J. Sci. Explor. 27(1) 13–23 (2013), p. 16 (Methods). Acrylic stress guidance: American Plastics Corp. acrylic data page (≤ 750 psi continuous); Plaskolite OPTIX-L fabrication guide (oversize holes, minimise stress); Perspex Design Guide §1.4.3; Röhm PLEXIGLAS machining guide 311-1 (annealing). Box work: /workspace/sim-lab/rod-fixtures (rev A HDPE), /workspace/sim-lab/rod-thermal/dipole-detector (DD-433/1296/2450), hub 8e53b6a (read-only). No Wolfram Cloud twin planned (analysis page). Numbers were computed in Python; the WL re-check is owed. Drafted 2026-09-28 by Grok Bot for Dan Britton.

text: Setup · 1.3 gigahertz (GHz) / 1296 megahertz (MHz) · not 8 GHz How to set up the Hively replication on the bench New: VNA guide for Steve: how to check the KB-1820 sphere feed, cables and the 23 cm filter with the VNA6000-A before a run. Different experiment (not this mesh tent): Monstein–Wesley 2002 brass-rod polarizer — monstein.html. Interactive 1296 MHz TEM vs SLW fields · First article for this Scalar Longitudinal Wave (SLW) hub. Primary radiator: K-Mac KB-1820 0.750″ (¾″) 3003 aluminum hollow sphere, fed by RG-405U, centre conductor soldered into a #76 pin hole, shield kept off the ball (corrected 5 Oct 2026, exp-1296.html#feed), inside two Less EMF RadioScreen mesh tents — TinySA Ultra 406 spectrum analyzer / signal generator in the detector tent, generator in the transmitter tent. Cricket/Cricut sticky-mat + bifilar pancake + sleeve-stub are archived (historical / optional control only) — #archive-bifilar. Numbers for that old path still match the lab protocol and coil calculator. Antenna shift (first article). Experiment A’s first-article antenna is the K-Mac KB-1820 0.750″ (¾″) aluminum hollow sphere, fed by RG-405U, centre conductor soldered into a #76 pin hole, shield kept off the ball (corrected 5 Oct 2026, exp-1296.html#feed). Unlike Experiment B, the shield must not touch this ball. At 1296.000 MHz / 23 cm. Cricket/Cricut sticky-mat + bifilar pancake + sleeve-stub are archived — collapsed under #archive-bifilar (historical / optional control only). Shop notes: #sphere-a · #sma-shop-a. Electrically separate from B. 23 cm amateur band, build on 1296.000 MHz. Licensed amateur radio only. No magnetron. Experiment A first article — K-Mac KB-1820 0.750″ hollow sphere Shift from bifilar pancake to a small aluminum Faraday ball at 1296.000 MHz. Feed corrected 5 Oct 2026: the sphere is the driven element. The RG-405U centre conductor is soldered into a #76 pin hole and the shield stops 3.0 mm short of the ball, never touching it; a shield bonded to the ball would make it a closed cap and short the antenna. Dimensions: exp-1296.html#feed. The SMA bulkhead notes below are superseded for Experiment A. Band and mesh tents stay Experiment A; do not share RF feed with the 433.59 MHz bench. Role Part Notes Radiator / shield shell K-Mac KB-1820 3003 alloy aluminum hollow balls, 10-pack, unpolished, 0.750″ (¾″) diameter. ~$36.40 / pack (user quote). Ships with no hole — shop drills the SMA clearance. (Only the 2.50″ KB-2016 on Experiment B ships with a pre-drilled ¼″ hole.) Catalog: k-mac-plastics.com/balls/hollow-metal-balls.htm. SMA bulkhead Amphenol 901-9875 SMA-F bulkhead crimp for RG-316 / LMR-100A (cable group B), 50 Ω. Already on the hub (RF Parts). Thread: 1/4-36 UNEF (¼″-36 Unified Extra Fine); major diameter ≈ 0.250″ (6.35 mm). ¾″ interior access is very tight for an interior locknut. Recommend the shop plan: (1) clearance hole + exterior flange / solder fillet + conductive bond to the shell, or (2) solder/weld a small boss then tap 1/4-36 UNEF into the boss (only if the boss is thick enough for ≥2–3 full pitches), or (3) use a bulkhead that can be nutted if they cut a temporary access. Thin hollow-ball walls usually cannot take a reliable tapped thread by themselves — say so plainly to the shop. Bifilar-pancake winding, lift-off, and sleeve-stub fixtures are archived under #archive-bifilar (historical / optional control). Keep them labeled in the log if you still run them. Machine-shop / install — SMA bulkhead on the ¾″ ball (copyable work order) Superseded 5 Oct 2026. This bulkhead plan bonds the coax shield to the ball, which shorts the antenna. Do not build it for Experiment A. Use the pin-hole feed: exp-1296.html#feed. Kept for the record. After install: verify with VNA6000-A S11 at 1296 MHz (kit.html#vna6000). Printable shop drawing (Exp A) Exp B sheet (2.50″) Applies to Amphenol 901-9875 and typical SMA panel bulkheads with 1/4-36 UNEF threads. Same thread facts also inform Experiment B’s 2.50″ ball (sphere.html#sma-install · monstein.html#bulkhead), but A’s ¾″ ID makes nut access harder. Preferred mount: drill a clearance hole through the wall + locknut/washer (nut-clamp), not tapping the thin stamped wall. KB-1820 (¾″) ships with no hole — the shop drills from solid. Do not confuse with Experiment B’s 2.50″ KB-2016, which ships with a pre-drilled ¼″ hole. A ¼″ (0.250″) hole is not a tap drill for 1/4-36 (it is ~thread major diameter). Preferred clearance: 6.5 mm / 0.256″ (often letter F ≈ 0.257″). Deburr so the O-ring/flange seats. Item Value Comment Thread 1/4-36 UNEF ¼″-36 Unified Extra Fine; major ≈ 0.250″ (6.35 mm) Preferred panel hole 6.5 mm (≈ 0.256″) Acceptable window ~6.3–6.6 mm; clearance + nut-clamp As-received hole None on KB-1820 Shop drills clearance from solid. (B’s KB-2016 has stock ¼″ — see sphere.html#sma-install.) Tap (conditional only) 1/4-36 UNEF 2B Only if wall or a welded/soldered boss is thick enough for ≥2–3 full pitches Tap drill (conditional) #3 (0.2130″) usual ~75% chart; some shops use #2 (0.2210″) in aluminum Confirm against the shop’s chart and the connector datasheet. Do not treat 0.250″ as the tap drill. Copy-paste work order (Experiment A · KB-1820) SUPERSEDED 5 Oct 2026: DO NOT BUILD. The shield must not touch the ball. See exp-1296.html#feed. WORK ORDER — Experiment A SMA bulkhead on K-Mac KB-1820 0.750″ 3003 Al hollow ball Part: Amphenol 901-9875 SMA-F bulkhead (1/4-36 UNEF), RG-316 / LMR-100A crimp. Goal: coax into interior; outer conductor / bulkhead body bonded to ball shell as shield. Frequency context: 1296.000 MHz / 23 cm (shop: mechanical only). NOTE: KB-1820 ships with NO hole. (Only Experiment B’s 2.50″ KB-2016 ships with a pre-drilled ¼″ hole.) PREFERRED (do this unless you add a thick boss): 1. Drill a clearance hole through the wall from solid: 6.5 mm (≈0.256″); window 6.3–6.6 mm (letter F ≈ 0.257″ is fine). Deburr both sides so flange/O-ring seats. 2. Nut-clamp: locknut + washer from the accessible side. On a ¾″ ball the interior nut is VERY tight — prefer exterior flange/solder fillet + conductive bond to the shell, or cut temporary access, or weld/solder a small boss first. 3. Bond: ensure RF-conductive bond between bulkhead body (outer) and aluminum shell. Feed: center conductor / crimped coax into the interior; shell is the outer/shield. DO NOT: - Tap the thin stamped hollow-ball wall as the primary plan. - Drill ¼″ (0.250″) thinking it is a 1/4-36 tap drill (0.250″ is ~major diameter; little/no material for threads). Prefer the 6.5 mm clearance above. CONDITIONAL TAP PATH (only if wall or a welded/soldered boss supports ≥2–3 full pitches): - Tap: 1/4-36 UNEF 2B - Tap drill: #3 (0.2130″) usual ~75% thread; #2 (0.2210″) sometimes used in Al for easier tapping. Confirm with shop chart + 901-9875 datasheet. - Thin hollow-ball walls alone usually cannot take a reliable tapped thread — say so plainly. What you are building Two mesh Faraday tents face each other on a wooden/plastic rail. First article: both tents hold a matching ¾″ KB-1820 sphere + Amphenol 901-9875 SMA bulkhead — generator in the TX tent, TinySA Ultra 406 in the RX tent (read through the see-through mesh). No coaxial cable (coax) between tents if you can help it — a cable is a leak. Range r is sphere-to-sphere (or bulkhead tip to bulkhead tip). Precision ranging: #ranging-a (Hively ask — keep RX out of the TX near field). Cricket/Cricut sticky-mat + bifilar + sleeve-stub are archived under #archive-bifilar. Precision TX–RX distance control (Experiment A) Hively wants a means of precision distance control for TX–RX separation. Experiment A uses matching ¾″ spheres in mesh tents — no polarizer rods (rods are Experiment B only). Near-field floors @ 1296.000 MHz (λ = 231.3 mm): reactive near field ≈ λ/(2π) ≈ 37 mm. For these electrically small balls, 2D²/λ is only a few millimetres and is not a useful floor. Conservative start for logged runs: ≳ 1–2 λ ≈ 0.25–0.5 m (about 10–20 in). Do not park RX inside the reactive zone. Paint hard marks on the rail at λ/(2π), 1λ, and 2λ. Rail: non-metallic (wood / fiberglass / HDPE). Fixed TX stop; sliding RX sled. No steel optical rail in the aperture between tents. Readout: engraved or taped mm/inch scale on the rail, and/or a handheld laser rangefinder (optical — does not put conductor between antennas). Log r every run (sphere-to-sphere or bulkhead tip to tip). Fine adjust: leadscrew or rack under the RX sled (±1 mm is plenty at these ranges). Do not: bridge TX–RX with coax on a “sealed” run; leave people in the stub/sphere near zone at elevated power. Shared ranging philosophy with Exp B (longer baseline): shop-drawing.html#sheet-ranging · Exp B polarizer support (rods): #sheet-support. Later seawater (not this land article): Tomilin 2021 used Tesla+sphere at 27.4 MHz in sealed immersed boxes — gaps vs Exp A/B and Nanuk land cases: kit.html#tomilin-gaps · library.html#tomilin-2021. Primary path: matching ¾″ spheres + SMA in both tents. Mesh is about 50–60 decibels (dB), not a soldered-copper “thousands of skin depths” can. Still a real Faraday test if seams and cables are honest. You can see the TinySA display through RadioScreen by design. Archived bifilar/sleeve control: #archive-bifilar. Transmitter (TX) First article: K-Mac KB-1820 ¾″ Al hollow sphere, fed by RG-405U, centre conductor soldered into a #76 pin hole, shield kept off the ball (corrected 5 Oct 2026, exp-1296.html#feed). Generator inside the TX tent. Licensed 23 cm; milliwatts. Archived sleeve-stub control: #archive-bifilar. Cage RadioScreen Mesh (Less EMF #1124-0, nickel over copper on polyester, 130 threads per inch (TPI), 4 ft × 54 in). Two tents from one piece. Receiver (RX) First article: matching ¾″ KB-1820 sphere + SMA bulkhead. TinySA Ultra 406 in spectrum-analyzer (SA) / Ultra mode inside the RX tent. Archived bifilar pancake: #archive-bifilar. Archived — Cricket/Cricut sticky mat + bifilar pancake + sleeve-stub (historical / optional control). First article is the ¾″ sphere — #sphere-a. Expand only if you still run the old path. Deep links to #mat, #fold, #lift, #dmm, #tinysa, #fixture, #sleeve, and #tx-fixture still work inside this block. The Cricket / Cricut sticky gummy board (optional control — bifilar path) A Cricut cutting mat (Cricket mat, gummy board) is the winding jig: each turn sticks, so 22/24 AWG magnet wire cannot spring off and knot. You are not cutting anything and you are not putting the coil in the machine. Which mat. Green StandardGrip. Blue LightGrip if a new green mat wants to peel enamel. Skip purple StrongGrip. Green 12×12 mat on corrugated cardboard. If brand-new and grabby, press a cotton T-shirt once and peel — tacky, not a glue trap. Mask everything except a ~50 mm circle with parchment. Draw inside diameter (ID) 6 mm and outside diameter (OD) 35 mm (0.15 λ at 1296 MHz). Optional 58 mm (0.25 λ). Plastic push-pin or nylon screw through the center into the cardboard. Pull any steel pin before radio-frequency (RF) tests. One spool in a mug to the side so it can rotate. You only need one spool now. Fold-in-half winding (no hub solder) — optional control Fold first. Cut one piece of 22 or 24 AWG magnet wire about 2.2 m (that is ~1.0 m per leg plus extra for leads). Fold it in half (gentle U, not a crease). The fold is the center — series-opposing, no hub solder. Park that fold at the 6 mm hub on the Cricut StandardGrip sticky mat, then wind both legs out together as a pair to OD 35 mm. The two free ends are the RF terminals. You never scrape or solder the midpoint. Not two separate wires. Gentle U-turn at the hub — do not knife-crease. A sharp fold can fracture the copper (open circuit) or crack enamel into the first turn. Optional Kapton on the bend. Measure 2.2 m. Mark the midpoint. Fold with a finger-radius, not a fingernail crease. Check the two free ends with a digital multimeter (DMM) before you wind (see next section). If it is already open, the fold broke the copper — cut a new piece. Tape the pair flat for 2 cm just outside the fold. No braid. A light twist (~1 / 3 cm) only if the pair splits; log it. Park the fold at the 6 mm hub on the gummy mat. Stick the first pair-turn. Wind outward, both legs at once, one layer, no daylight between turns. Count pair-turns. Stop at 35 ± 1 mm. Photo against a ruler. Leave ~80 mm free ends. Stop. Photograph the pancake still on the mat, ruler in frame. Then lift it off as its own procedure — lift off the sticky mat — so the fold does not spring open. The fold method makes series-opposing only. For an aiding / transverse-electromagnetic-loop control, wind a second pancake as a single-filar of similar OD, or two wires paralleled. Label them. Lift the fold-in-half pancake off the Cricut StandardGrip mat — optional control Winding is done. The gummy board did its job: 22/24 AWG stayed planar and did not knot. Now you have to get the coil off the mat without spring-out, enamel cracks, or opening the hub fold. This is a handling step, not a new winding method. Do not peel from a free end or from the fold. A yanked lead will telescope the spiral; a yanked fold can crack copper the digital multimeter already said was continuous. Leave the mat on the cardboard. Do not flex the mat first — bending the gummy board stores spring that dumps into the pancake. Slide a plastic card (old gift card, scraper, or Cricut spatula) under a mid-radius pair-turn, not under the hub and not under the outer free ends. Keep the card almost parallel to the mat. Work around the spiral in short arcs. The pair should release as a flat disk. If a turn jumps, park it with a fingertip and resume from the opposite side — do not chase it with tweezers. When the disk is free, lift it as a plate: two fingers under opposite outer turns, fold still a gentle U. Do not open the fold, do not flatten it into a crease, do not let the two legs scissor. Isopropyl alcohol (IPA) on a lint-free cloth: wipe adhesive residue off the enamel. Do not soak the fold. Do not scrape enamel on the spiral or the hub — scrape only the two free ends, and only after the pancake is on its fixture. Digital-multimeter continuity again, free-end to free-end, leads zeroed. Same pass band as the table below. Flex the fold gently; OL (open circuit) means rewind. Photograph the meter with the pancake in frame. That photo is the “survived lift-off” check. If the mat still grabs, a drop of IPA at the card edge can release a turn. Wait for the alcohol to flash off before the next radio-frequency run so you are not measuring wet polyester adhesive. Expected resistance and open-circuit check Copper resistivity at 20 °C: AWG 22 ≈ 0.0530 Ω/m, AWG 24 ≈ 0.0842 Ω/m. Current walks the entire 2.2 m (out one leg, through the fold, back the other). What you measure AWG 22, 2.2 m AWG 24, 2.2 m Verdict Copper only (calculated) ~0.12 Ω ~0.19 Ω Physics, not the digital-multimeter reading yet Digital multimeter on the 200 ohm (Ω) range, test-lead resistance zeroed 0.15–0.40 Ω 0.20–0.50 Ω Pass — fold is continuous Digital multimeter reads OL (overload / open loop — meaning open circuit), infinite, or no continuity beep Broken copper at the fold, or a lead not scraped Fail — open circuit. Rewind. Digital multimeter reads ~0.00 Ω even with leads zeroed, and the spiral is unused You are probing a dead short at the terminals (the two free ends touching) Separate the ends and remeasure Zero the digital multimeter by touching the probes together. Write that offset down (~0.1–0.3 Ω is common on cheap leads). Scrape 5 mm of enamel off each free end. Tin if you like. Measure free-end to free-end. Subtract the lead offset. Compare to the table. Flex the fold gently. The reading must not jump to OL (open circuit). If it does, the copper is cracked — rewind with a larger bend radius. Photograph the digital multimeter. That photo is the error check that the fold did not open-circuit the wire. A digital multimeter cannot see a hairline enamel puncture mid-spiral. It can catch the failure that matters for fold-in-half: a fractured U-turn. Continuity after winding, again after mounting, and again after the first radio-frequency run. TinySA Ultra 406 and impedance — skip the matching resistor on the detector The TinySA Ultra+ ZS406 (4″ screen, SubMiniature version A (SMA) connector, 50 ohm) is a 2-in-1: spectrum analyzer and signal generator. The spectrum-analyzer input is specified 50 Ω when internal attenuation is ≥ 10 dB. Frequency: 100 kilohertz (kHz)–900 MHz normal, Ultra mode to ~5.4–6 GHz — so 1296 MHz receive is in Ultra mode, which is fine. Generator caveat. Clean sine output is only specified to ~800–900 MHz. At 1296 MHz the Ultra 406 generator is in the square-wave / mixer region (harmonics and spurs). If it is the transmitter source, enable Ultra, add a 23 cm bandpass after the SMA connector (buy list: ZX75BP-1307-S+ or DEM-BPF), log that it is not a clean sine, and stay licensed. Ultra RF is SMA-F even though the brass threads are on the outside; you screw an SMA-M plug onto those threads. One TX-path filter is enough; the RX TinySA does not need this BPF unless you add a second later. A 23 cm transverter or brick is the cleaner transmitter; the TinySA is the better detector. Do not put a 47–51 Ω resistor in series with the bifilar on the detector. The pancake is ~0.2 Ω of copper. A 51 Ω series resistor in front of a 50 Ω TinySA is a ~6 dB (factor-of-four in power) pad that throws away the already-tiny detected voltage. Hively’s “match the coil resistance to the source” is a transmit remark for a coil whose R was designed near 50 Ω. This 35 mm fold-in-half article is not that coil. Idea Use it? Why TinySA input, atten ≥ 10 dB, shortest SMA pigtail (short coaxial jumper) Yes — default The instrument already is 50 Ω. Short leads beat a matching network you have not characterized. 51 Ω series at the pancake (detector) No Kills signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Does not make the coil a 50 Ω antenna; it just pads. 51 Ω shunt across the pancake No, first article Dumps detector current into the resistor. 1:1 RF transformer (e.g. Mini-Circuits ADT1-1+ / TC1-1) if you have one Optional second article A balun (balanced-to-unbalanced transformer), not a pad. Log S11 (input reflection) if a vector network analyzer (VNA) shows up later. 47 Ω thin-film (not wirewound) in series at the generator SMA Only if the Ultra 406 is the transmitter and you want it to see ~50 Ω Protects the generator from a near-short. It is a pad on transmitter power, not a detector match. Document the extra 6 dB. Internal low-noise amplifier (LNA) on TinySA Try both, log it 20 dB low-noise amplifier, noise figure (NF) about 5 dB. Off for strong-signal / overload checks. Never exceed +6 dBm (decibels relative to one milliwatt) at 0 dB internal attenuation. Keep the SMA jumper from pancake to TinySA under 10 cm. Ferrite on that jumper if you see cable-pickup that dummy-loading does not kill. Mount the pancake on a semi-permanent non-metallic fixture — optional control The coil does not live on the Cricut mat for radio-frequency work, and it should not sit loose in the mesh tent. Give it a rigid, non-metallic plate that keeps the pancake planar, carries a short SMA pigtail, and can be lifted in and out of the RadioScreen tent without crushing seams. Plate. Acrylic, HDPE, plywood, or a 3D-printed PLA/PETG disk/rectangle larger than 35 mm (something like 80–100 mm across). No copper-clad, no steel washers in the RF path. The pancake stays one layer, face-on, not warped into a dish. Hold-downs. Nylon screws, plastic clips, Kapton, or hot-glue dots at a few outer points. Do not cinch steel hardware through the hub. Do not use the fold as a mounting loop. SMA pigtail. Shortest practical jumper from the two scraped free ends to the TinySA Ultra 406 — under 10 cm. Strain-relieve the coax on the plate so a tug hits the fixture, not the enamel. No 51 Ω series resistor on this detector (see TinySA section). TinySA on the same sled (optional but tidy). Velcro or a plastic cradle so the 406 and the pancake move as one assembly. Screen still faces a mesh wall so you can read it from outside. Inside the tent. Slide the fixture in through the flap; do not stuff it through a seam. The mesh must close with a 50 mm overlap. The plate must not tent the cloth or pinch a corner. The fixture is removable: out for continuity checks, packing, and photos; in for sweeps. Fasteners in the cage. Nylon/plastic only on the sled. Clothes-pins, wood battens, or plastic clamps for the flap. No steel binder-skeleton sitting next to the pancake if you can help it — keep ferrous hardware off the RF path. Continuity one more time after the SMA is on the plate. Log “pancake on fixture, pigtail < 10 cm, nylon hardware.” Photograph the assembly next to a ruler before the first sealed run. Sleeve balun (not a skirt) — novice how-to — optional control Full manufacturing guide (BOM photos, fit note on McMaster 8965K22, build steps, IARD reference slides): sleeve-balun.html. This was the Experiment A historical / optional control build at 1296.000 MHz — now archived. Patent language may stay historical; the hardware you solder is a close-fitting sleeve, not US 9,306,527 Fig. 2A’s fat skirt. Primary first article is the ¾″ sphere (#sphere-a). Patent (historical). Fig. 2A is an annular skirt balun: larger diameter than the coax outer, extends backward from the feed, outer conductor tied to the top of the skirt. The patent says that λ/4 path cancels return current on the outside of the tubular second conductor and also acts as a small ground-plane/counterpoise (currents on the center conductor and the outside of the skirt both +Z). That fat skirt can launch extra TEM. Build (this hub). Hively 2026 personal communication (paraphrase only; no private email): build a sleeve balun, not a skirt, for the 1.3 GHz replication. Sleeve (bazooka choke): close-fitting λ/4 conductive tube over the coax jacket, soldered to the shield at the end away from the stub tip, open at the feed/tip. Same choke physics (λ/4 shorted line → high Z for common-mode), but it does not add a large-diameter radiating skirt. No 3λ ground disk. Experiment B’s 433 MHz balls use no balun — do not copy these steps onto monstein.html. Numbers: λ = 231.3 mm; λ/4 sleeve = 57.8 mm in air (trim if the sleeve–jacket gap has VF < 1); first-article stub = λ/10 = 23.1 mm of center conductor (λ/4 = 57.8 mm remains the TEM-style control stub). RG-405/U or SMA pigtail. Brass/copper tube snug over the jacket. 23 cm BPF still in the TX chain inside the Faraday wrap (#bpf). Side view: coax → solder ring at the cold end of the sleeve → 57.8 mm sleeve → open at the feed → 23.1 mm stub. Tube is snug over the jacket, not a fat radiating skirt. Install SMA (or use an SMA pigtail) on the generator end of RG-405/U in the ordinary way. Cut a brass/copper tube that is a snug slide over the jacket, a little longer than 57.8 mm so you can trim. ID clears 0.086″ with only a thin gap — this is a sleeve, not a large-diameter skirt. Strip the jacket so 23.1 mm of center conductor is the first-article stub (or 57.8 mm if you are running the TEM-style λ/4 control stub). Do not add a 3λ ground disk. Slide the tube on. Solder a ring to the shield at the cold end (away from the stub tip). Leave the feed/tip end of the sleeve open — no solder bridges there. If the sleeve–jacket gap has VF < 1, trim shorter than 57.8 mm. Photograph the fillet and the open end next to a ruler. 23 cm BPF still in the TX chain inside the Faraday wrap: Ultra SMA-F → filter SMA-M → filter SMA-F → SMA-M stub (#bpf). Mount this assembly on the TX sled below. Packing: foam around the 23.1 mm stub so it cannot get bent. Shared submersible cube (later) is kit.html; Pelican 1200 remains the small travel case. Matching TX fixture (sleeve-balun stub + generator) — archived optional control Do the same idea on the transmitter side so the two tents are portable twins, not a permanent bench sculpture. The TX tent still holds the sleeve-balun stub and the generator; they just ride a second non-metallic sled. Non-metallic plate or small wood block sized for the RG-405 sleeve-balun stub, the 57.8 mm sleeve, and the generator (TinySA in generator mode, brick, or transverter). Nylon/plastic fasteners only in the RF path. Stub tip remains the range origin: when you measure tent-to-tent distance, it is still stub tip to pancake face. Mark that axis on the rail. Short SMA / semi-rigid on the generator. If the Ultra 406 is the source: 23 cm bandpass between the Ultra and the SMA-cable TX stub (#bpf — SKUs stay in the shopping list). Chain stays inside the TX Faraday enclosure: Ultra SMA-F → filter SMA-M → filter SMA-F → SMA-M stub. Log square-wave / mixer-region output, optional 47 Ω only at the transmitter SMA. Licensed milliwatts; no magnetron. Slide the TX fixture into its RadioScreen tent the same way as the RX sled: flap open, fixture in, overlap closed, no crushed seams, no USB cable out on a sealed run. The TX fixture is removable for dummy-load swaps, photos of the 23.1 mm stub, and packing. Do not hard-tape the generator to the mesh. RadioScreen mesh Faraday cages (Less EMF) Product: RadioScreen Mesh, Less EMF (electromagnetic field products) part 1124-0. Nickel over copper on polyester (23.4% copper, 10.9% nickel, 65.7% polyester), 130 threads/inch, 0.09 mm, 54 in wide. Dan’s piece: 4 feet, $83.80. Lab-quoted attenuation: about 50–60 dB from 10 MHz–1 GHz, still >25 dB into the fifth-generation (5G) cellular bands. Surface resistivity < 0.1 Ω/sq. See-through, which is why the TinySA display can be read from outside. Honest dynamic range. 60 dB is not Hively’s 25,000 dB copper-pipe claim. Mesh is a Faraday screen: plenty to knock transverse-electromagnetic leakage down for a first look, not a skin-depth fortress. Publish it as a mesh-cage test. A later soldered-copper can is a different (stronger) article. If a tone survives 60 dB of mesh and the dummy-load / transverse-electromagnetic-antenna controls, that is still worth ink — just do not call the mesh 2885 skin depths. Best practices for this cloth Two tents from 4 ft × 54 in. Cut two ~2 ft lengths. Each wraps a cardboard or wood frame (~30×30×30 cm is enough for a TinySA + ¾″ sphere or generator + sphere; archived bifilar/stub also fit). Overlap the closing flap by at least 50 mm. Seams, not the weave, are the leak. 130 threads-per-inch openings are ~0.2 mm (≪ λ/100 at 1296 MHz). The closing flap is a removable seal: conductive hook-and-loop, binder clips on a wood/plastic batten, or magnets on a non-metallic strip — 50 mm overlap, then clamp. Do not make the flap a permanent 3M 1181 / conductive-fabric-tape weld; you need to open this tent every run and pack it. Clothes-pins or wood battens still count. No steel wool “maybe.” You cannot easily solder this mesh (polyester core). Clamp, sew with conductive thread, or use removable conductive hook-and-loop. Grounding: Less EMF wants the mesh grounded for household use. For two experiment cages, bond each tent to itself; do not run a long ground wire between tents (that wire is a dipole). Optional single-point earth, logged. No cables out during a “sealed” run. A Universal Serial Bus Type-C (USB-C) cable to a laptop is an antenna. Run the TinySA on battery. No charging cable. If you must have a cable, it is a slotted / leaky config, not sealed. Instruments inside. Transmitter generator in the transmitter tent (contains its own transverse-electromagnetic leakage). TinySA in the receiver tent, screen facing a mesh wall so you can read it. The TinySA’s local oscillator also radiates — that is now inside the detector cage. Log “spectrum analyzer inside” as the default; one control run with the TinySA outside and a short feedthrough tells you whether the local oscillator (LO) is talking to the detector (sphere first; archived bifilar if used). Looking through the mesh is allowed and is the point of RadioScreen. Don’t press your face into a gap. Don’t unzip to peek “just for a second” mid-sweep. Corners and floors. Mesh on the bench without a floor is an open box. Wrap five or six sides. A cardboard carton as the skeleton, mesh around it, copper-tape the joins. Roll, don’t crease leftover cloth (Less EMF: permanent creasing). Keep it dry; wipe, don’t launder. Order of first measurements First article: matching ¾″ KB-1820 spheres + SMA in both tents; generator in TX, TinySA in RX (Ultra mode, atten ≥ 10 dB). Measure r sphere-to-sphere (or bulkhead tip to tip). Archived sleeve/bifilar path: #archive-bifilar. License, identify, milliwatts (or TinySA generator with a 23 cm filter). Do not camp on 1296.100. Control matrix: open (flap up), slotted (flap half-lapped), sealed (50 mm overlap, clamped / hook-and-loop — not a permanent copper-tape weld), dummy_load (SMA dummy instead of radiator), 90deg, tem_negative (small loop in place of the sphere). CSV log on Lab. Decision rule. A leftover tone that dies when you dummy-load the transmitter is leakage or pickup. A leftover tone that beats the TEM-loop and single-filar floors, with both flaps sealed and no USB cables, is the result you publish — whatever it is. Quote mesh attenuation in decibels, not copper skin depths. Packing and shipping: Lady Lake, FL then Middletown, RI The whole experiment should pack as one kit: both RadioScreen tents, two ¾″ sphere + SMA assemblies (TX/RX), TinySA Ultra 406, generator, cables, and clips. First destination is bench time in Lady Lake, Florida; later the same bags go to a demo in Middletown, Rhode Island. Build so you can zip it, fly or drive it, and put the rail back together. Archived bifilar/sleeve hardware only if you still run that control — #archive-bifilar. Mesh. Open the tents, pull the fixtures out, then roll the RadioScreen (Less EMF: do not crease — a fold is a permanent leak line). Slip each roll into a labeled bag or tube. Keep leftover cloth rolled with the tents. Spheres (first article). Cap SMA, foam around each ¾″ ball so the bulkhead cannot bend. Optional archived pancake: leave it on its rigid plate in foam; do not put the coil back on the Cricut mat for travel (mat is a winding jig only — see #archive-bifilar). TinySA Ultra 406 in its own case. Cap the SMA. No USB cables left attached — not to the TinySA, not dangling from a power bank, not “already plugged in for the next site.” Same rule for the generator. A small pick-and-pluck case (Pelican 1200 class; see shopping list) holds the RX plate in foam plus the flap clips if you want one outer shell. TX sled. Sphere + SMA (and generator) on a non-metallic plate; foam around the ball. Dummy load rides in the same bag. Archived sleeve-stub plate only if you still pack that control. Labeled bags. Suggested split: RX-sphere+SMA, TX-sphere+gen, mesh-tents, TinySA-406, cables+clips, DMM+IPA+card. Print a paper inventory in the outer case. Flap hardware in the clips bag: conductive hook-and-loop, binder clips, wood/plastic battens, magnets for removable seals. Clothes-pins. Measuring tape for tent-to-tent r. Archived Cricut StandardGrip mat only if you expect to rewind the optional bifilar; otherwise leave it home. Removable flap seals travel; a copper-tape weld does not. Do not pack by wrapping the tents in 3M 1181 or conductive fabric tape “so they stay shut.” Both tents rolled (not creased), two frames or cartons if you use them Both ¾″ spheres + SMA capped, in foam TX/RX fixtures + dummy load padded (archived sleeve/pancake only if packed) TinySA Ultra 406 in case, SMA capped, battery charged, USB disconnected Generator / filter / attenuators bagged and labeled SMA pigtails (< 10 cm on the detector), ferrites, nylon hardware Conductive hook-and-loop, binder clips, magnets, clothes-pins — flap kit License, ID plan, CSV log / notebook, ruler, IPA, plastic card Inventory sheet: Lady Lake, FL bench first; Middletown, RI demo later — same kit Short shopping list (verified links) Exact product pages used to kit the fixture and travel case. Open in a new tab. Do not treat this as an endorsement beyond “this is the SKU we checked.” Licensed 23 cm / 1296 MHz only. First-article radiator: KB-1820 sphere — see #sphere-a. ¾″ Al hollow spheres (first article). K-Mac KB-1820 0.750″ 3003 aluminum hollow, 10-pack unpolished (~$36.40 / pack, user quote): k-mac-plastics.com/balls/hollow-metal-balls.htm. Machine-shop clearance / tap notes: #sma-shop-a. Coil / TX plates (archived bifilar / optional fixtures only). Amazon 6×6×1/8″ acrylic: Amazon 6×6×1/8 acrylic (B0B4BKRJT5); 6-pack: Lesnlok acrylic 6-pack (B0C3V3JCXD); TAP Plastics cut-to-size: TAP clear acrylic sheets, cut to size; McMaster HDPE 12×12×1/8″: McMaster HDPE 12×12×1/8 (5865N111). Cricut StandardGrip mat (archived / optional control only). Only if you still wind the bifilar path under #archive-bifilar. Green StandardGrip 12×12; not a cutting job — winding jig only. Soften: skip unless you need the historical control. Nylon fasteners (no steel in the RF path). McMaster nylon standoffs; 4-40 nylon pan-head screws: McMaster 4-40 nylon-6/6 pan-head screws. SMA pigtail, about 10 cm, male–male. ALLiSHOP SMA extension ~10 cm M–M (B07YHJ9L7T). SMA bulkhead (Amphenol 901-9875). TestEquity 901-9875 SMA bulkhead. Removable flap seal — conductive hook-and-loop, not permanent copper tape. Less EMF conductive hook-and-loop fastener. RadioScreen mesh (two tents from one piece). Less EMF RadioScreen mesh. Travel foam for the coil plate / clips. Pelican 1200 with pick-n-pluck foam — small TinySA / coil travel case, not the submersible TX hull. The cube hull is on kit.html. 23 cm bandpass — TX path only (TinySA Ultra as generator). Drop-in SMA ceramic BPF between the Ultra generator and the SMA-cable TX stub. Purpose: kill square-wave harmonics/spurs from the Ultra at 1296 MHz. Keep the whole string inside the TX Faraday enclosure. One filter on the TX path is enough; the RX TinySA does not need this unless you add a second later. Licensed milliwatts; no magnetron. Primary (drop-in SMA, ~$108, stock on Mini-Circuits): Mini-Circuits ZX75BP-1307-S+ ceramic BPF, 1215–1400 MHz, 50 Ω (datasheet PDF). Connectors: INPUT SMA-MALE, OUTPUT SMA-FEMALE. TinySA Ultra RF jack is SMA-FEMALE (not male). Ultra RF is SMA-F even though the brass threads are on the outside; you screw an SMA-M plug onto those threads. Chain: Ultra SMA-F → filter SMA-M → filter SMA-F → SMA-M stub (short SMA/semi-rigid). Cheaper ham option, Live Oak, FL, $40, 1–2 weeks (low-level / milliwatt class, matches TinySA): Down East Microwave DEM-BPF — select Frequency 1296 MHz and Connector SMA. May be SMA-F both ends; then a short SMA-M/M barrel or pigtail to the Ultra. Keep USB cables in the cables bag, not attached. Roll RadioScreen; nest the ¾″ sphere (and optional pancake plate) in the Pelican foam. Flap seals are hook-and-loop / clips / magnets — not 3M 1181 welded shut. Different experiment (not this mesh tent): 433 MHz polarizer spheres/rods shopping list is on monstein.html#parts — not the Experiment A kit. Interactive TEM vs SLW (JS canvas) The 1.3 GHz TEM vs SLW + SNR cartoon is the 2D canvas on fields.html — not a Wolfram Cloud embed. Printable checklist First article: two K-Mac KB-1820 ¾″ Al hollow spheres, each with a #76 pin hole 2.5 mm deep for the RG-405U centre conductor; shield 3.0 mm off the ball, never touching (feed dimensions) Measure r sphere-to-sphere or bulkhead tip to bulkhead tip on the non-metallic rail TinySA Ultra 406: spectrum-analyzer / Ultra mode, attenuation ≥ 10 dB, battery, no USB cable; LNA on and off logged NanoRFE VNA6000-A: SOLT-calibrated S11 of each ¾″ sphere feed (+ BPF S21) before sealed runs — kit.html#vna6000 If Ultra 406 is also the generator: 23 cm filter (#bpf), log square-wave mode, optional 47 Ω at the transmitter SMA connector only TX sphere + generator on a portable fixture in the TX tent; matching RX sphere + TinySA in the RX tent Two RadioScreen tents, 50 mm overlaps, removable flap seals (hook-and-loop / clips / magnets — not permanent copper tape), no cables out when sealed Read the 4″ display through the mesh; don’t open the flap mid-sweep Control matrix + CSV log; license and identify on the air Pack kit for Lady Lake, FL then Middletown, RI: roll mesh, spheres in foam, TinySA in case, USB off Shopping list SKUs on this page: KB-1820, nylon, SMA pigtail, bulkhead, hook-and-loop, RadioScreen, Pelican 1200 (small travel case, not the submersible hull), 23 cm BPF Archived optional control only (#archive-bifilar): Green StandardGrip mat / fold-in-half bifilar / lift-off / sleeve-stub — not the first article. Skin-depth tables and CSV logger: Lab. Lengths: Tools. Mesh: lessemf.com/product/radioscreen-mesh. TinySA specs: tinysa.org Ultra specification. B-field null · Tekbox probes (on hand) For any Exp A sphere listen aimed at Scalar Longitudinal Wave (SLW) / Scalar Wave (SW) language: use the Tekbox H20/H10/H5 magnetic probes near the receiver to check presence/absence of B (Hively guidance; IARD_2020 / 2016-era notes). Protocol and kit specs: kit.html#tekbox. Without B knowledge, do not claim “SLW/SW not TEM.”

text: Machine-shop drawings — SMA bulkhead on Al hollow spheres Printable sheets for mounting Amphenol 901-9875 (SMA-F bulkhead, 1/4-36 UNEF) on catalog 3003 aluminum hollow balls. Feed philosophy: coax into the interior; bulkhead body / outer conductor bonded to the shell as shield (Monstein–Wesley style). That applies to Experiment B only: for Experiment A the shield must not touch the ball (corrected 5 Oct 2026, exp-1296.html#feed), so Sheet A is superseded. Educational; licensed amateur RF only. Print all sheets A text work order B sphere install B rods cut/deburr B support + rotator A+B precision ranging Hole facts: Exp A KB-1820 (¾″) ships with no hole — shop drills from solid. Exp B KB-2016 (2.50″) ships with a pre-drilled ¼″ hole — do not tap that hole as a 1/4-36 tap drill. Preferred clearance for both: 6.5 mm (≈ 0.256″). Sheet A — Experiment A · 1296 MHz · KB-1820 0.750″ Superseded 5 Oct 2026. The bulkhead and flange below bond the coax shield to the ball (shell = shield), which shorts the antenna. Do not build this sheet. Corrected feed: #76 (0.020″) pin hole 2.5 mm (0.10″) deep, centre conductor soldered in, 1.5 mm (0.06″) PTFE exposed, shield cut end 3.0 mm (0.12″) off the ball and never touching it. Dimensions: exp-1296.html#feed. Project SLW Hub Exp A · Faraday mesh tents · 1296.000 MHz (shop: mechanical only) Date 2026-09-16 Ball K-Mac KB-1820 · 0.750″ (19.05 mm) OD · 3003 Al hollow · no as-received hole Qty 2 (TX + RX) Connector Amphenol 901-9875 SMA-F bulkhead · 1/4-36 UNEF · RG-316 / LMR-100A crimp Flange (opt.) 6061-T6 or soft Al washer/boss — recommended starting values below Preferred path (A), superseded 5 Oct 2026 Use the pin-hole feed instead (exp-1296.html#feed). Old text: Exterior flange/boss + Ø6.5 mm clearance through flange and wall + conductive bond of 901-9875 body to shell. Avoid relying on an interior locknut (¾″ ID is too tight). MW manufacturability note Monstein & Wesley Fig. 1 used a machined ball with an 18 mm shaft and 34 mm base (thick feed). Our flange/boss is the catalog-ball analogue: thicken the feed region so the SMA can be mounted without tapping a thin stamped wall. Not a full Fig. 1 remachine. Sheet B — Experiment B · 433.59 MHz · KB-2016 2.50″ Project SLW Hub Exp B · Monstein–Wesley ball + polarizer · 433.59 MHz (shop: mechanical only) Date 2026-09-16 Ball K-Mac KB-2016 · 2.50″ (63.5 mm) OD · wall ~0.132″ (3.35 mm) · 3003 Al · stock ¼″ hole Qty 2 (TX + RX) Connector Amphenol 901-9875 SMA-F bulkhead · 1/4-36 UNEF · RG-316 / LMR-100A crimp Flange (opt.) Same starting values as A if nut-clamp is awkward Preferred path (B) Keep/ream to Ø6.5 mm clearance + locknut/washer.
