text: Simulation Lab report · home sources (motors) · faithful HTML conversion NOTE.md — Home AC compressor and blower motors as SLW sources? (inrush vs running current) Are home AC compressor and blower motors plausible SLW sources? Inrush vs running current, Hively's own charging-current criterion, ranked sub-events (PWM edges, contactor arcing, capacitor switching), a measurement plan, and the literature survey. MIXED ← Simulation Lab catalogue Provenance /workspace/sim-lab/home-motors/NOTE.md (last modified 2026-09-26 06:51 EDT) /workspace/sim-lab/home-motors/LIT.md (last modified 2026-09-26 06:51 EDT) Converted to HTML 2026-09-28 (EDT) as a faithful conversion: text, numbers, equations and labels are the source's own. No new equations were added; only the TEM tags described below and the edits listed here were made. Status lines inside the source (for example "nothing published", "HELD", "draft") describe the state when it was written. This page is its GitHub Pages twin, published 2026-09-28. No Wolfram Cloud twin planned (analysis/report page, not one of Experiments A–G). Numbers are Python-computed; WL compare OWED where the source says so. Framing rules on this page (Dan). Under the SLW hypothesis no skin-depth, permeability, ferromagnetic or cage shielding-effectiveness argument is used to rank or dismiss SLW/SW. The Faraday cage strips TEM noise (FACT); an SLW passing the cage wall is HYP. Every passage that uses transverse-EM (TEM / classical / cage-SE) reasoning is tagged transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis. FACT / HYP / ASSUMPTION labels are kept exactly as in the source. Downloads home_motor_numbers.json Simulation Lab · home-motors · 2026-09-26 · literature and reasoning only (nothing sent or published; SYNC_LEDGER.md untouched) Labels. FACT = textbook, measured, datasheet or standard. HYP = Hively, Monstein or scalar-wave hypothesis. ASSUMPTION = our modelling choice or reasoning. Equations. No new equations. The only equations used are: Hively US 9,306,527 EQN. 15, P_OUT = (I²/4π)·√(μ/ε) (HYP); Zhu et al. 2022 Eq. (3), i_b = C_b dv_b/dt; NEMA MG 1 §12.36, as a ratio. Arithmetic (sinusoid peak slope ωI_pk, and I_pk = √2·I_rms) is elementary calculus, labelled ASSUMPTION (sinusoidal current). Files: home_motor_numbers.py and home_motor_numbers.json (illustrative numbers); src/ (downloaded datasheets and PDFs with text extracts). 0. SUMMARY (verdict) Is inrush magnitude itself a plausible HYP SLW source? No, by Hively's own written criterion. Hively ties the SLW to an irrotational charging current where current must stop: US 9,306,527: "essentially all of the electrical current goes into charging and discharging the antenna"; Hively & Reed 2020 p. 11: "charge accumulation causes arcing across the fault; this gradient-driven current creates the SLW." A motor winding is a closed inductive loop, so its inrush and running currents are solenoidal. Hively's own writing gives circulating currents zero SLW (Hively & Reed p. 9; Hively & Loebl App. C). Consistency check (ASSUMPTION, using HYP EQN. 15). If the whole motor current counted, a 5-ton compressor's 31.6 A running current would emit ≈30 kW of SLW. Its electrical input is only ≈5.5 kW. At 178 A LRA the figure would be ≈0.95 MW. Only a small charging fraction can be Hively's I. The inrush (FACT). About 6× running current for 100–300 ms (Copeland AE4-1331 p. 16). The first half-cycle peak is 1.8–2.8× the rms symmetrical value (NEMA MG 1 §12.36). Peak slope only ~10⁵ A/s, all at 60 Hz. That is the least HYP-relevant part, and the part Dan's TinySA can't see. Sub-events ranked by HYP relevance (charging into open ends, gaps or capacitance, i = C dv/dt): Inverter PWM edges in ECM blowers (e.g. 20 kHz, TI TIDA-01353) and variable-speed compressors. dv/dt up to 10 kV/µs (Zhu 2022). Common-mode charging of winding-to-frame capacitance, continuous while running. Contactor or relay arcing. Showering-arc bursts with <10 ns rise, repeating at 10 kHz–1 MHz. This is Hively & Reed's arcing case. Start and run capacitor switching. Lumped ±Q, so weak (ASSUMPTION). 60 Hz line and winding-to-ground charging. The 60 Hz inrush envelope. Last. Microwave oven. SLW emission from an oven is HYP. Its most HYP-like element is the magnetron's open-ended output probe at 2.45 GHz, plus a 4 kV doubler. Its "switching" is 60 Hz gating, or 20–50 kHz in inverter ovens. So it shares the fast-dv/dt ingredient with ECM blowers, not with compressor inrush. Detection. Motor energy sits at 60 Hz–kHz, below the TinySA (100 kHz and up) and the Zeenko amps (~10 MHz and up). A copper-mesh cage gives only ~5–23 dB of magnetic shielding even at 10–150 kHz (Kühn 2013), and less at 60 Hz. False-positive risk is therefore high. The discriminating test (§4): inside the closed cage, battery-powered LF E (sphere plus preamp) and LF H (search coil) channels; event times from a current logger or microphone outside; pass only if E rises without H, beyond the calibrated cage transfer ratios. The house-wiring and cage simulation is owed (§5). Literature verdict (details in LIT.md, searched 2026-09-26): (a) No measurement ties SLW or SW to motors, compressor inrush or inductive switching. Not peer-reviewed, not even self-published. (b) Nothing compares magnetron switching with motor inrush. The scalar-wave literature uses microwave ovens as unpowered Faraday cages (Meyl kit, HYP), not as sources. The only "oven as SLW source" document is Dan's own July 2026 planning page (SPECULATION). (c) Hively and the Keyport patent name arcs and sparks as SLW drivers: fault arcing (Hively & Reed 2020 p. 11), lightning and tape-peeling arcs (Hively & Land 2021 p. 2), a "resonant spark system" (US 12,525,711 claim 30). All HYP, none measured. Motors appear only as superconductor applications (Hively) or as receiver loads (Meyl, Handwerker). An EED-internal preprint (Rentzber, arXiv:2608.19405, HYP) finds that charge-conserving sources give C = 0. If that holds, even arcs and PWM do not source the SLW unless local charge conservation fails. Net: the ranking above rests on reading Hively's criterion, not on any observation. 1. AC compressor starting 1.1 Facts (cited) Inrush ratio and duration (FACT). Copeland Application Engineering Bulletin AE4-1331 R9 (Sep 2024), p. 16, "Single Phase Starting Characteristics": "The starting Locked Rotor Amperage (LRA), also referred to as inrush current, is normally six or more times higher than the rated running amperage of the compressor and lasts from 100 to 300 milliseconds until the rotor starts turning." p. 23: "'inrush current' and locked rotor amps (LRA) are one and the same." The nameplate LRA is measured on a locked compressor at the highest nameplate voltage, read after four seconds. 5-ton example (FACT, datasheets). Copeland ZP57K5E-PFV (R-410A, 208–230 V, 1-phase, 57,000 Btu/h): LRA 178 A and RLA 31.6 / 28.3 A (Baker Distributing and WalkairDirect listings); AHRI-rated input 5460 W at 25.5 A (Copeland ZP-series sheet, dkkarani.com PDF); so LRA/RLA ≈ 5.6 and LRA/rated current ≈ 7.0 (home_motor_numbers.json); three-phase variants: ZP57K5E-TF5 LRA 136 A; -TFD (460 V) LRA 66.1 A, RLA 9.7 A (Sigler listing; Copeland ZPK5 service-kit table). Note (FACT vs premise): the single-phase 5-ton LRA (178 A) sits above Dan's "~100–150 A" range. Three-phase or 460 V units fall inside or below it. The "3–8× RLA" range is consistent with Copeland's "six or more". Asymmetric first half-cycle (FACT). NEMA MG 1-2016 Part 12, §12.36 "Instantaneous Peak Value of Inrush Current": "The values in the previous tables are rms symmetrical values ... There will be a one-half cycle instantaneous peak value which may range from 1.8 to 2.8 times the above values as a function of the motor design and switching angle." The DC offset depends on the point-on-wave at contact closure. Start components (FACT). AE4-1331 p. 16: "Start assist devices are usually not required"; PTC start devices "rated from 10 to 25 ohms may be used". p. 18: "A start kit (specified start capacitor and relay)". Single-phase scrolls use a run capacitor (e.g. ZR57K3-PFV: run cap 80 µF / 370 V, optional start cap 270–324 µF / 330 V; Copeland technical spec sheet). ASSUMPTION (general HVAC practice, uncited): a potential relay drops the start capacitor out once the motor is up to speed. That is a contact opening in a capacitor circuit. Contactor arcing (FACT). EMC Compliance training note "Transient susceptibility" (emccompliance.co.uk): "When a current is interrupted by an unsuppressed electromechanical switch (either a manual switch, contactor or relay) the resultant voltage rise across the gap causes a repetitive ignition and extinction of an arc discharge – the so-called 'showering arc' effect ... The burst repetition rate varies from 10kHz to 1MHz ... Typically the rise time of each strike is less than 10ns and the duration is tens to hundreds of ns; transit time is roughly 5ns/m." It also says these transients "couple along the supply circuit or are radiated from the conductors on either side of the switch" and "decay with distance". ASSUMPTION: bounce on closure (with the 6× inrush) and arcing on opening both occur at the condenser contactor. Inverter / variable-speed compressors (FACT). Danfoss "Inverter scroll compressor VRJ, Application Guidelines" (residential, R-410A), p. 8: "With VRJ compressors, the LRA value is low because the variable speed drive reacts very rapidly (far below 1 second)." The table lists VRJ028 at LRA 10.2 A versus MCC 18 A, so LRA is below the running maximum: no across-the-line inrush. The PWM drive is the trade-off: carrier kHz to tens of kHz, edges to MHz (Zhu et al., IEEE Access 10, 125279–125280, 2022: PWM "several kHz up to tens of kHz", "dv/dt, typically up to 10kV/µs", EMI "several to tens of MHz"). 1.2 Spectral content and slopes Inrush: 60 Hz carrier with a 100–300 ms envelope step plus a decaying DC offset. Peak slope of 178 A rms: ≈9.5×10⁴ A/s. At the NEMA half-cycle peak (320–498 A): ≈1.2–1.9×10⁵ A/s, treating that peak as a sinusoid amplitude. Running (31.6 A): ≈1.7×10⁴ A/s. Label: ASSUMPTION arithmetic, home_motor_numbers.json. This is "slow" (~10⁴–10⁵ A/s). The envelope change adds sidebands within a few Hz to tens of Hz of 60 Hz (ASSUMPTION). Contactor arc: broadband, ns rise, 10 kHz–1 MHz burst rate (FACT, above). ASSUMPTION: with hundreds of volts to kV across the gap in <10 ns, dv/dt ≳10¹⁰–10¹¹ V/s. Inverter PWM: dv/dt up to 10 kV/µs = 10¹⁰ V/s (Zhu). Wide-bandgap example: 400 V in 25 ns ≈ 1.6×10¹⁰ V/s (Scelba et al., IEEE TIA 58, 4461, 2022, test conditions). 1.3 Coupling to Hively's HYP source term Hively's criterion (HYP, quoted in /workspace/sim-lab/sub-sources/MECHANISM.md): Hively & Loebl 2019 p. 123: "The irrotational current density (JL) is maximal at the feed point ... and zero at the end of the antenna (z = L)." US 9,306,527: "essentially all of the electrical current goes into charging and discharging the antenna". Hively & Reed 2020 p. 11: "charge accumulation causes arcing across the fault; this gradient-driven current creates the SLW." Hively & Reed 2020 p. 9: "A TEM transmitter produces only circulating currents, yielding C = 0 and EL = 0 with no SLW power output or reception." transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis Motor winding (ASSUMPTION reasoning on HYP). The winding is a closed loop from line to line (or line to neutral). Current enters and leaves; no charge accumulates. Inrush magnitude therefore scales a solenoidal current, which gives no SLW under HYP. Candidate HYP-relevant pieces (ranked in §0): (a) contactor or relay arcing, the gap-charging and breakdown case; (b) common-mode charging of winding and cable capacitance to the grounded frame, i = C dv/dt (Zhu Eq. 3). At 60 Hz this is small. With PWM edges it is large (Scelba et al. 2022: "the fluctuation of the common-mode voltage generates currents that flow to the ground through parasitic capacitances between the stator windings and the motor frame. The amplitude of such currents depends on the rate of variation of the common-mode voltage and increases with switching frequency"); (c) start and run capacitors. Charge does accumulate there, but as ±Q on closely spaced plates, which is dipole-like and closed by displacement current. ASSUMPTION: by analogy with Hively's App. C, whose balanced dipole gives no SLW output, a lumped capacitor is a weak HYP source compared with an unbalanced, monopole-like charging path to ground. EQN. 15 internal-consistency flag (ASSUMPTION using HYP). Put P_OUT = (I²/4π)·√(μ/ε) with √(μ₀/ε₀) = 376.73 Ω: Current EQN. 15 result 178 A (LRA) ≈950 kW 31.6 A (RLA) ≈30 kW 7 A (PSC start) ≈1.5 kW 1.5 A (PSC run) ≈67 W The RLA figure exceeds the compressor's 5460 W input, which violates energy conservation. So I in EQN. 15 cannot be the motor's supply current. It can only be the irrotational charging component, consistent with Hively's own definition. Same flag as the sub-sources MIL-STD-1399-300B case: a 20 A capacitive line-to-ground current gives ≈12 kW. A testable prediction for HYP: if even 1 A of common-mode charging current were fully "gradient-driven", EQN. 15 predicts ≈30 W of SLW from every VFD-equipped appliance. 2. Indoor blower: PSC vs ECM PSC (FACT). A PSC motor keeps the capacitor winding in circuit continuously. Beckett Technical Bulletin "An Introduction to PSC Motors" (Oct 1999), p. 1: "Both the capacitor (auxiliary) winding and the main winding remain in the circuit the entire time the motor is running, hence the name 'permanent'." Table 1 (1/7 hp PSC burner motor, a close analogue of a small blower): starting (locked-rotor) current 7 A vs running 1.5 A, i.e. ≈4.7×. That is higher than the "~2–3×" in the prompt. Blower-specific PSC LRA data were not found; see Blockers. PSC motors start across the line through a relay in the furnace control, so inrush is at 60 Hz (ASSUMPTION: same physics as §1.2, at ~1/25 the current). Relay arcing also applies. ECM (FACT). TI reference design TIDA-01353 (TIDUCE0A), "Electronically Commutated Motor Reference Design for HVAC Blowers" (½ hp, 115 V AC): spec table p. 2: "Inverter switching frequency 20 kHz", DC link 163.5 V typical; the intro contrasts it with "a permanent split capacitor motor, or PSC"; §2.2.3.5–2.2.3.6: open-loop start-up where "the START_UP_DUTY parameter is gradually increased to START_UP_DUTY_MAX", a soft start. Power Integrations RDR-872 (70 W fan inverter) lists 10 kHz PWM. The carrier is manufacturer-specific. The furnace's 100 Hz–1 kHz "PWM" airflow command is a low-voltage control signal, not the power switching (hvac-fanmotor.com guide; low-authority source, FACT only for the distinction). ECM consequences: little inrush (soft start; plus the DC-link capacitor inrush at power-up, limited by an NTC or thermistor in typical designs, as in RDR-872 "inrush thermistor RT1"). But there are continuous fast PWM edges and common-mode currents to ground while running. This is the HYP-favoured ingredient (Zhu Eq. 3; Scelba et al. 2022). 3. Comparison table (device vs HYP source) ⚠ Rows/columns in this table that refer to TEM / classical / cage SE: transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis Device / event Peak current dI/dt, dv/dt Spectral content Where charge accumulates (HYP source per Hively) Classical TEM / near-field emission (FACT unless marked) Field geometry Compressor inrush, fixed-speed 5-ton 178 A rms LRA; half-cycle peak 320–498 A (NEMA 1.8–2.8×) ~10⁵ A/s (60 Hz slope) 60 Hz plus 100–300 ms envelope plus DC offset Nowhere significant. Closed winding loop (solenoidal). Small 60 Hz charging to frame. 60 Hz magnetic field from supply loop and motor (∝ current, loop area); 240 V E-field from wiring Quasi-static dipole-like B near cables and motor; kr ≪ 1 (λ = 5000 km) Compressor running 31.6 A RLA ~1.7×10⁴ A/s 60 Hz plus harmonics As above As above, ~6× lower B As above Contactor / relay arcing (compressor, PSC blower) Transient; set by line impedance (unquantified here) <10 ns rise; ASSUMPTION ≳10¹⁰ V/s Broadband, bursts at 10 kHz–1 MHz rate, content to ~100 MHz (ASSUMPTION from <10 ns rise) Across the opening gap: charge builds, then breaks down. The Hively & Reed "arcing" case. Conducted and radiated bursts that "decay with distance" (EMC Compliance note); visible to TinySA (≥100 kHz) and to a radio as clicks Local to wiring; transmission-line-like along house wiring Start cap / hard-start relay; run cap Start-cap charging current up to LRA-class during start (ASSUMPTION) 60 Hz, plus a relay-opening transient 60 Hz plus a switching burst ±Q on capacitor plates (lumped, dipole-like; weak per ASSUMPTION §1.3) Small, local Confined between plates Inverter compressor / ECM blower PWM Motor current (ECM ½ hp: a few A); CM current to ground unquantified here dv/dt up to 10 kV/µs (Zhu); 1.6×10¹⁰ V/s WBG example Carrier 10–20 kHz (RDR-872, TIDA-01353) to tens of kHz, harmonics to tens of MHz Winding-to-frame and cable-to-ground capacitances, charged every edge (i = C dv/dt, Zhu Eq. 3). Unbalanced to ground, monopole-like (ASSUMPTION). Conducted and radiated CM EMI (Zhu "several to tens of MHz"); CM current on leads and ground CM loop through ground: antenna-like at MHz PSC blower start ≈4.7× running (7 A vs 1.5 A, Beckett 1/7 hp) ~4×10³ A/s 60 Hz Closed loop; run cap ±Q 60 Hz B, small Quasi-static Microwave oven, transformer type (comparison; SLW emission is HYP) Magnetron anode 330 mA avg, 1.5 A peak max; 4.40 kV peak anode (LG 2M246 datasheet); "half-wave doubler with leakage transformer" HV swings of kV at 60 Hz; conduction gated to half of each 16.7 ms cycle (IEEE 802.11-98/240) 60 Hz gating; 2.45 GHz RF (~50 MHz swept) Magnetron output probe, an open-ended monopole into the waveguide at 2.45 GHz (textbook HYP geometry but inside a closed metal cavity); HV doubler capacitor and cathode at −4 kV 2.45 GHz leakage ≤1 mW/cm² new, ≤5 mW/cm² thereafter, at ≥5 cm (21 CFR 1030.10(c)(1)); 60 Hz transformer stray B Contained cavity plus door-seal leakage; far field at 2.45 GHz in air Microwave oven, inverter type Similar anode; IGBT primary current IGBT switching at 20–45 kHz (Panasonic service literature; "about 20 to 50 kHz", Panasonic US 8,492,687) 20–50 kHz plus harmonics; 2.45 GHz As above, plus the 20–50 kHz resonant HV transformer charging As above, plus kHz CM EMI As above EQN. 15 probe for the magnetron (ASSUMPTION): 0.33 A → ≈3.3 W; 1.5 A → ≈67 W. The same caveat applies: the anode current is a closed-circuit current, not an open-end charging current. 4. Detection with Dan's gear, and a discriminating test 4.1 Why the current setup is blind or false-positive-prone for motors (FACT + Dan's gear) Frequency coverage. Motor inrush energy lies at 60 Hz–kHz. The TinySA Ultra's normal range starts at 100 kHz, and the Zeenko amps are not usable below ~10 MHz (per Dan's gear note). Only contactor-arc bursts and the upper PWM harmonics fall in band. Those are classical broadband EMI that the TinySA will see if anything leaks. Cage magnetic shielding is poor at low frequency (FACT). Kühn, John & Weigel, Adv. Radio Sci. 11, 189 (2013), measured a closed copper-mesh enclosure (30×30×10 cm, overlapped mesh) at 10–150 kHz. Magnetic SE was "very low (from 5 dB to 23 dB in the frequency range to be considered)" in one orientation, and ~20 dB higher in the other. transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis They note measured values run ~22 dB below the Kaden analytical model, due partly to imperfect seam connections. Magnetic (eddy-current) shielding falls with decreasing frequency (their Fig. 3/5 behaviour). At 60 Hz a thin non-ferrous mesh gives little H shielding. The electric field, by contrast, is strongly shielded: the paper says "the incident electrical field could be neglected due to Faraday cage effect". Resulting false-positive path (ASSUMPTION). 60 Hz or kHz H-field from the compressor supply loop leaks into the cage. It induces EMF in any loop formed by sphere, preamp, battery and leads. That EMF looks like a "sphere signal inside a Faraday cage". Vibration at compressor start (microphonics, triboelectric cable noise) is a second path. 4.2 Proposed discriminating test (literature-based design; not run) Goal. Look for an E-channel response inside the closed cage, time-locked to motor start events, without a matching H-channel response. Its size must exceed what the measured cage transfer ratios predict classically. The cage strips TEM (FACT for TEM). SLW passing the wall is HYP. transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis Outside the cage (event timing and reference): Start-event timestamps. Preferred and non-invasive: a clamp-on AC current logger on the condenser or air-handler supply. Use a split-core CT on a single conductor at an accessible point, installed by a qualified person if any panel or disconnect cover must be opened, with a battery logger sampling ≥1 kHz. Alternatives: a microphone or accelerometer on the condenser, or a light sensor on the blower status LED. Either gives start times to ~ms without touching mains. Outside E and H reference sensors near the cage: LF E-probe (a short monopole or plate into a high-impedance preamp) and an LF search coil, logged on the same clock. Inside the closed cage (battery-powered; no cable crosses the wall; data out by fiber or SD card): 3. E-channel. Existing KMAC sphere into a high-impedance, low-noise LF preamp (FET buffer, 10 Hz–100 kHz; specific part TBD) into a battery 24-bit recorder (96–192 kHz sampling covers 10 Hz–~90 kHz). Also, or instead, an Airspy HF+ Discovery (Expt D shopping list: HF coverage 0.5 kHz–31 MHz per airspy.com, as quoted in expt-d/web/slw-detectability.html) behind an LF preamp, for the kHz–MHz PWM and arc bands, on a battery host with fiber out. H-channel. A multi-turn LF search coil or a battery fluxgate/ELF magnetometer on the same recorder. The Tekbox H20 loop is too small for 60 Hz sensitivity (ASSUMPTION). Control channels (same recorder): a dummy sphere (same size, disconnected or terminated); a shorted-input preamp; an accelerometer (to flag vibration). Clock sync. Sync before closing the cage, plus a fiber-coupled LED flash as a shared marker. GPS will not work reliably inside the cage. Procedure. (i) Calibrate outside-to-inside transfer ratios for E and H using a known LF source (a Helmholtz or loop coil for H, a plate for E) at 60 Hz, 1 kHz, 20 kHz and 100 kHz, following the Kühn 2013 method. (ii) Log ≥50 compressor and blower start/stop events. Include ECM run periods, and inverter-compressor periods if fitted. (iii) Epoch-average around each event. (iv) Classical prediction: inside E ≈ outside E × (E transfer, tiny); inside H ≈ outside H × (H transfer, near 1 at 60 Hz); sphere EMF explained by H pickup in its loop and by vibration. (v) HYP-supporting outcome: a sphere E response not explained by the H-channel times the loop pickup, absent on the dummy sphere and shorted input, not correlated with the accelerometer, and repeatable across cage rotations. (vi) Repeat with the cage moved farther from the supply run. Classical H falls with distance from the wiring loop. Equipment to add (ASSUMPTION list; prices and parts not checked): Airspy HF+ Discovery; LF high-impedance preamp; battery 24-bit audio recorder or DAQ; LF search coil or fluxgate; battery current logger with split-core CT (or a microphone logger); fiber LED sync link. 4.3 What TinySA can still do now Watch 100 kHz–30 MHz for contactor-arc bursts and ECM PWM harmonics, inside and outside the cage, time-locked to start events. Anything seen inside is first a cage/seam/cable leak (VERIFY.md steps in /workspace/sim-lab/sub-sources/) before it is anything else. 5. Simulation owed (not run) Logged as OWED; not run, because a credible model needs house-wiring geometry and cage/seam details we don't have. Quasi-static magnetic model, 60 Hz–100 kHz (Elmer FEM magnetodynamics, or FEMM for 2-D). Inputs: compressor supply loop (line/neutral spacing, run length, 178 A inrush / 31.6 A run) and the ECM CM current path. Output: H at Dan's cage location. Mesh-cage LF shielding model. Magnetic and electric transfer ratios of Dan's actual mesh and 3–4-wrap rolled seam at 60 Hz–100 kHz, including seam contact resistance. Validate against the Kühn 2013 measurement style. Pickup model. EMF induced in the sphere/preamp/battery loop by the leaked H. This gives the classical false-positive level. openEMS full-wave, 1–100 MHz. Contactor-arc and PWM-harmonic radiation from house wiring into the cage (EFT-like 5/50 ns source, per the IEC 61000-4-4 test waveform; exact waveform numbers are from a search snippet, see Blockers). Literature survey (LIT.md) Source heading: LIT.md: literature search on motors, compressor inrush, inductive switching and microwave ovens as scalar / longitudinal-wave sources Simulation Lab · home-motors · 2026-09-26 · literature only. No one was contacted, nothing was published, and SYNC_LEDGER.md was not touched. No equations are introduced here. Labels Evidence labels (as defined for this task): FACT: published, peer-reviewed measurement. HYP: published claim or hypothesis, not independently replicated. Peer-reviewed theory and self-published experiments both fall here. SPECULATION: no experimental backing (books, forums, blogs, marketing, planning documents). Direction column: pro-SW: claims a scalar or longitudinal effect. null/classical: finds an ordinary explanation. theory: no measurement. context: not about sources. Local copies are in src/lit/. Earlier local texts are in /workspace/ohmic-slw-search, /workspace/hively-monstein and /workspace/hub/papers. 1. Category verdicts (short) (a) Experimental detection of scalar/longitudinal waves from motor starting, compressor inrush or inductive-load switching: nothing found. No peer-reviewed or self-published measurement ties a scalar or longitudinal wave to a motor start, compressor inrush or contactor/relay switching. The closest items are: one self-published spark-gap experiment on the propagation speed of a collapsing Coulomb field (Gasser 2016, HYP). It is not a motor or an inductive load. Hively's and the Keyport patent's designation of arcs and sparks as SLW drivers (HYP, no measurement). the Tesla-derived "radiant energy" thesis that abrupt DC interruption across a spark gap emits a longitudinal ray (Lindemann 2001, SPECULATION). (b) Literature comparing magnetron switching with motor inrush as scalar-wave sources: nothing found. No paper, patent or report compares the two. In the scalar-wave literature the microwave oven appears as an unpowered Faraday cage (Meyl's kit manual; Meyl Docu §VII "The mobile phone in the microwave"), not as a source. The only document proposing a microwave oven as an SLW source is Dan's own planning page, "Proposed Experiment: Hively and Microwave Oven" (July 2026). Its basis is extrapolation from Hively's 8 GHz reports; it contains no measurement (SPECULATION). (c) Mentions by named researchers of motors, compressors, inductive switching or household appliances as candidate sources: None names motors, compressors or household appliances as SLW/SW sources, with one exception: Meyl's generic claim that "technical devices" radiate longitudinal vortex waves (electrosmog book blurb, SPECULATION). Hively mentions "electric motors and generators" only as applications of high-temperature superconductors (US 9,306,527, cols. 17–18). Hively's closest source statements are about arcing: seismic arcing across a fault (Hively & Reed 2020, p. 11), lightning and tape-peeling arcs (Hively & Land 2021, p. 2). The Keyport sleeve-balun patent claims a "resonant spark system" feeding the antenna (US 12,525,711 B1, claim 30). Meyl and Handwerker use motors only as loads driven by Tesla-coil receivers. A 2026 arXiv EED paper (Rentzber) states that charge-conserving sources, including all ordinary circuits, give C = 0 and no scalar-longitudinal radiation, even within extended electrodynamics. That excludes motors, arcs and PWM unless local charge conservation fails (theory, not peer-reviewed). Hub pages. No hub page presents a microwave oven as an SLW source. Every hub copy (hub-efield-repo, hub, slw-hub) states "No magnetron source in this hub's lab protocol". This appears in library.html, learn.html, compare.html, future-scalar-ab.html, sw-vs-slw.html and c-nuclei*.html. lab.html says "no magnetron, no microwave oven, no 8 GHz TWT as the primary source" and "No modified microwave oven in this protocol". monstein.html says "13 cm (2.45 GHz ISM / ham segments) only if you replicate. No magnetron protocol." index.html links Dan's oven page as "Proposed oven experiment (historical; this hub does not use a magnetron)". The only basis for "oven as source" in the hub ecosystem is that linked planning page (SPECULATION). 2. title: Corrections log: charge-relaxation exponent (author-confirmed)
headings: Where the hub uses or quotes it
description: Corrections log (2026-09-30): the printed exponent E = E0 e^(-epsilon t/sigma) in Hively & Loebl 2019 Eq. A5 and US 9,306,527 col. 5 has epsilon and sigma swapped; the author confirmed E = E0 e^(-sigma t/epsilon), tau = epsilon/sigma. FACT, author-confirmed.
text: Simulation Lab · corrections log · 2026-09-30 Corrections log: charge-relaxation exponent (author-confirmed) The transient in Hively & Loebl 2019 and in US 9,306,527 is printed with ε and σ swapped. The author confirmed the correct form on 2026-09-30. This page records the correction and where the hub uses it. FACT, author-confirmed ← Simulation Lab catalogue Author-confirmed, 2026-09-30. In a private email from Dr. Hively to Dan (2026-09-30), Dr. Lee Hively confirmed the form of the charge-relaxation transient: "The form, E = E0 e^(-sigma t/epsilon), is the correct one." What is corrected TYPO as printed Hively & Loebl, Phys. Essays 32, 112 (2019), Eq. (A5), p. 122, prints E = E0 e^(−εt/σ). TYPO as printed US 9,306,527 B1, col. 5, the exponent before EQN. 12, prints E = E0 exp(−εt/σ). In the patent the permittivity glyph is ∈. FACT, author-confirmed Correct form: E = E0 exp(−σ t / ε), with relaxation time τ = ε / σ. ε and σ are swapped in the two printings above. FACT, author-confirmed Hively & Land, IARD 2020, slide 60, prints E = Eo e^(−σt/ε). That slide is correct. Units check FACT σ is in S/m and ε in F/m, so ε/σ is in seconds and σt/ε is dimensionless. The swapped form εt/σ would have units of s² and cannot sit in an exponent. FACT Arithmetic, τ = ε/σ: seawater with εr = 80 and σ = 4 S/m gives 80 × 8.854×10⁻¹² / 4 = 1.8×10⁻¹⁰ s. The hub's submarine survey gets 1.51×10⁻¹⁰ s with its seawater model at 60 Hz (σ = 4.29 S/m). Copper, ε0/σ with σ = 5.8×10⁷ S/m, gives 1.5×10⁻¹⁹ s, matching the ∼10⁻¹⁹ s the 2019 paper states beside Eq. (A5). FACT This is a transient in time (charge relaxation). It is not a path loss over distance, and it does not by itself give an SLW attenuation constant. Under the SLW hypothesis the only loss term the hub uses is the Joule term σE∥² (or none, under the 2022 Erratum toggle). Where the hub uses or quotes it Page Status experiment-c.html (#ohmic) Correct form E = E0 exp(−σt/ε), τ = ε/σ since hub PR #58 (2026-09-26). Author-confirmed note added 2026-09-30. Joule-loss positions Quotes the printed (A5) and patent forms verbatim; both are now labelled as typos. Author-confirmed note added. Submarine SLW/SW source survey Quotes slide 60 (correct). Two open items about the hub exponent marked resolved. Author-confirmed note added. experiment-c-snr.html, sleeve-balun-snr.html No relaxation transient is computed on these pages (the Ohmic path factor is exp(−α L), a spatial factor). Short pointer to this log added. Only the single sentence above is quoted from the email. Nothing else from the email is reproduced here. Paper and patent references: library. See also: three readings of SLW loss (Mode C uses this relaxation form) and the equation source and meaning map.

The TinySA Ultra and the Tekbox E5/H10 probe: existing equipment. Cage estimate (CAGE_ESTIMATE.md) Source heading: Dipole Detector (DD-433 / DD-1296 / DD-2450): Faraday Cage Estimate (Rev A, 2026-09-27) Grok Bot initial estimate for Dan Britton. Please verify before buying or cutting. Numbers come from cage/cage_estimate.py → cage/cage_numbers.json. Units are mm, with inches in parentheses. Labels: FACT (cited) · CLASSICAL-TEM (textbook Maxwell/TEM result, kept separate from SLW) · RULE OF THUMB · ASSUMPTION · HYP (SLW hypothesis). Nothing here uses TEM attenuation to rank or dismiss SLW. transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis 0. What goes in the cage, and the one hard rule The Dipole Detector is an instrument, not an experiment. It gets its own sealed cage, separate from the bifilar-coil cage, the Experiment B (433.59 MHz M&W) polarizer array and the oven. Inside the cage: one Dipole Detector variant on its HDPE plate: DD-433 (433.59 MHz, Experiment B), DD-1296 (1296 MHz, Experiment A) or DD-2450 (2.45 GHz oven test) the SMA jack and about 300 mm (12 in) of coax with the sleeve balun TinySA Ultra on its internal battery (about 100×60×30 mm, 4×2.4×1.2 in) the Tekbox E5/H10 near-field probe Dan's standing rule: no cable crosses the cage wall. That means no feed-through, no bulkhead connector and no penetration of any kind. Data leaves in one of two ways: saved on the TinySA (e.g. to its microSD card, if your unit has one; ASSUMPTION, check) and read after opening, or an optical link through a waveguide-below-cutoff (WBC) tube (§6). ASSUMPTION: the dipole sits in the middle of the cage. Clearances below are measured from the cut-long length of 0.47λ, which is the longest rod you would put in. 1. Why the walls must stay back from the dipole RULE OF THUMB (labelled): a conducting wall closer than about λ/2 to 1λ noticeably detunes and loads a dipole. It shifts the resonant frequency and changes the feed resistance. CLASSICAL-TEM background: Balanis, Antenna Theory (linear wire antennas, "ground effects" section), treats a horizontal dipole a height h above a conducting plane with image theory. Its input impedance swings around the free-space value and settles toward it as h grows past roughly λ/2. The specific λ/2–1λ threshold above is the rule of thumb, not a quoted figure. transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis CLASSICAL-TEM: a closed box is also a cavity. Its resonances are at f = (c/2)·√((m/a)² + (n/b)² + (p/d)²) (Harrington 1961 §6-9 / Balanis AEE §10.4, as cited in the hub). transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis When the cage is many wavelengths across it is "overmoded": the field inside depends on position. So every dipole reading is calibrated in its own cage, at a fixed position. A cage-loaded resonance is acceptable as long as it is measured and recorded. 2. Option 1: cage for DD-2450 and DD-1296 Variants: DD-2450 is 57.5 mm (2.26 in) with λ = 122.4 mm; DD-1296 is 108.7 mm (4.28 in) with λ = 231.3 mm (0.47λ cut-long lengths used for clearance). Cube inside size 2450: tip gap 2450: side gap 1296: tip gap 1296: side gap Lowest cavity mode Verdict 300 mm (11.8 in) 121 mm = 0.99λ 150 mm = 1.23λ 96 mm = 0.41λ 150 mm = 0.65λ 707 MHz 2450 only, marginal. Not for 1296. 450 mm (17.7 in) 196 mm = 1.60λ 225 mm = 1.84λ 171 mm = 0.74λ 225 mm = 0.97λ 471 MHz Good for 2450; borderline for 1296. 600 mm (23.6 in) 271 mm = 2.22λ 300 mm = 2.45λ 246 mm = 1.06λ 300 mm = 1.30λ 353 MHz Recommended. At least 1λ from every wall at both bands. Tip gap is (cube − dipole)/2, i.e. from each rod tip to the end wall. Side gap is cube/2, from the rod to the side walls. CLASSICAL-TEM, cavity modes: transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis The 600 mm cube has 578 modes below 2450 MHz, with 27 of them within ±1% of 2450 MHz. It has 95 modes below 1296 MHz, including one at 1298.1 MHz (+0.17%). I searched 450–650 mm boxes: at these frequencies mode spacing is about 1% or less, so mode avoidance is not practical. Calibrate in-cage instead. Optional: a few pieces of RF absorber foam in the corners lower the cavity Q and make readings depend less on position. This is CLASSICAL-TEM practice; price unverified. transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis 3. Option 2: cage for DD-433 (433.59 MHz) DD-433 is about 325–346 mm (12.8–13.6 in) long, λ = 691.4 mm (27.2 in); clearances use 325 mm (0.47λ). Inside size (long axis along the rod) Tip gap Side gap Nearest cavity mode to 433.59 MHz Verdict 400×200×150 mm 38 mm = 0.05λ 75 mm = 0.11λ none below 838 MHz Too small. The rod would be heavily detuned (walls < 0.1λ away). 900×450×450 mm 288 mm = 0.42λ 225 mm = 0.33λ 471.1 MHz (+8.7%) Workable only with in-cage calibration. 1000×600×600 mm (39.4×23.6×23.6 in) 338 mm = 0.49λ 300 mm = 0.43λ 463.4 MHz (+6.9%) Recommended. About λ/2 clearance, no mode near 433.59. 1200×600×600 mm 438 mm = 0.63λ 300 mm = 0.43λ 432.7 MHz (−0.2%) Avoid. A cavity mode sits right on 433.59. 1200×700×700 mm 438 mm = 0.63λ 350 mm = 0.51λ 431.6 MHz (−0.5%) Avoid, for the same reason. 1300×650×650 mm 488 mm = 0.70λ 325 mm = 0.47λ 415.7 MHz (−4.1%) Good, just bigger. Recommendation: use a 1000×600×600 mm box. Even there the side walls sit at about 0.43λ, inside the λ/2–1λ rule-of-thumb zone. So DD-433 must be characterized in-cage: measure its resonance and SWR inside the closed cage. Use a battery VNA inside, or TinySA plus a generator plus a return-loss bridge, or HackRF. Record the data, then open the cage. Cut the rod to resonate in-cage, or accept and record the cage-loaded resonance. Bonus: the same 1000×600×600 box also serves DD-1296 and DD-2450 with large clearance (all figures from cage_numbers.json): 1296 MHz: 1.93λ at the tips, 1.30λ at the sides. 2450 MHz: 3.85λ at the tips, 2.45λ at the sides. One cage could therefore cover all three variants. 4. Materials (pros and cons) Opening-size rule (RULE OF THUMB, common EMC guideline): every hole or gap should be much smaller than λ, typically ≤ λ/20: 2450 MHz: 6.1 mm 1296 MHz: 11.6 mm 433.59 MHz: 34.6 mm All the meshes below have openings of about 1.3 mm or less, so the mesh itself is fine. In practice seams and the door leak first, not the mesh. Material Openings Pros Cons Price (see §8) Aluminium window screen (Phifer 18×16, 0.010 in wire) ≈1.2–1.4 mm (derived from mesh count and wire) Cheap, easy to get, one 1220 mm × 7.6 m (48 in × 25 ft) roll covers either option Can't be soldered. Wire crossings oxidize and contact is uncertain, so seams need clamped overlaps and conductive tape. Floppy. $41.55 per roll (Home Depot, verified) Copper mesh, 16 mesh (TWP, 0.011 in wire) 1.30 mm (TWP datasheet) Solderable seams, good conductivity, stiffer than screen Costs more; sharp edges; tarnishes (only cosmetic if the seams are soldered) TWP "from $10.00"; per-foot price for 36 in width not shown (unverified) Copper filter mesh 100×100 (McMaster 9224T395/396/397/398, 36 in wide) 0.15 mm Very fine, solderable Harder to work, pricier; overkill for these frequencies McMaster price not shown online (unverified) Solid aluminium sheet (e.g. 24×36 in) none Best mesh-free wall; rigid Not solderable; seams need rivets or screws every few cm plus tape; heavy; can't see inside about $19.99 per 24×36 in sheet (search listing, unverified) Ni-Cu ripstop fabric (Less EMF #11213, 42.5 in wide) woven fabric Light and fast: sew or tape it into a bag or tent; fold-over closure Can't be soldered; seams by conductive tape or folding; crease wear from $14.95 per linear ft (Less EMF); $17.00 per ft (FilterEMF) Ni-Cu fabric (Faraday Defense CYBER NC-RS, 54 in wide) woven fabric Same as above, wider Same as above $24.99 per ft Shielding-effectiveness figures, vendor datasheet numbers only: Less EMF Ni-Cu Ripstop: 80 dB average from 10 kHz to 40 GHz; 80–94 dB at 700 MHz–2.7 GHz; 38–92 dB at 2.4–40 GHz; tested to IEEE 299-2006; 0.03 Ω/sq. LBA/Faraday Cyber NC-Berry: 75 dB average from 100 MHz to 18 GHz. Faraday Defense NC-RS: >55 dB from 10 MHz to 3 GHz. These are flat-sheet material numbers. A built cage is usually limited by its seams and door. No vendor SE figure was found for the window screen or the copper meshes, so none is quoted. transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis Frame: wood (1×2 or 2×2 in) or PVC pipe. A non-metal frame is fine near the dipole. Put the frame outside the mesh, or at least keep metal hardware at the corners, away from the rod. Recommendation: 16-mesh copper with soldered seams for the best result. Ni-Cu fabric is the fastest build. Aluminium screen is the cheapest but has the weakest seams. 5. Seams, door and hardware Wall seams: Overlap adjacent panels by 20–50 mm (0.8–2 in). On copper mesh, solder along the whole seam, or run copper foil tape over it and solder the tape edges. Where you can't solder (aluminium, fabric), use conductive-adhesive copper foil tape on both sides of the seam and press it hard. Vetco VUPN2321 copper tape, 2 in × 33 ft, conductive acrylic adhesive, $20.95 (verified). Do not rely on Less EMF aluminium tape for seams: its adhesive is synthetic rubber, so it is not a conductive joint. Door (lid): Make one face a separate lid with a 50 mm (2 in) lip that folds down over the walls. Contact must be continuous, not spot clamps: gaps between contact points act as slots. At 2450 MHz, λ/20 is only 6 mm. Choices: (a) EMI finger stock (beryllium-copper) around the opening, or (b) a conductive fabric-over-foam gasket, or (c) the lip pressed flat along its full length by a wooden batten on each side, clamped at both ends. Part numbers and prices for finger stock and gaskets were not verified. Fabric version: make it a bag with a roll-down closure (fold at least 3 times) clamped flat, like a dry bag. That is the simplest door. Other hardware: plastic spring clamps 60–100 W soldering iron and rosin-core solder (for the mesh) tin snips staple gun, or nylon zip ties to hold mesh to the frame (keep staples at the frame corners, away from the dipole) an HDPE shelf or Lazy Susan for the dipole plate 6. Grounding CLASSICAL-TEM: a closed conducting shell with no penetrations shields the inside whether or not it is connected to earth. An earth wire adds nothing to the shielding here. transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis Earthing is optional, for static or safety only. An earth wire must not enter the cage. If you add one, bond it to the outside skin only. 7. IR-thermometer hole (waveguide-below-cutoff tube) Source flag: the hub repo (/workspace/hub-efield-repo) has no WBC-tube guidance. The only related hub item is the TM01 stovepipe, λ_cut ≈ 23.23 cm. The formula below is the one already used in sim-lab (/workspace/sim-lab/expt-d/rxchain/REPORT.md §2), which cites H. W. Ott, Electromagnetic Compatibility Engineering, Wiley 2009: FACT (Ott): a circular tube of inner diameter d has TE11 cutoff f_c = 1.841·c/(π·d), about 176/d GHz with d in mm. Well below cutoff it attenuates about 32 dB per tube diameter of length. Tube Inner diameter Length f_c f/f_c at 2450 Attenuation (32 dB × L/d) 3/4 in Type L copper water tube (OD 0.875 in, ID 0.785 in, copper.org Table 14.2b) 19.94 mm 80 mm (3.15 in) 8.81 GHz 0.28 ≈128 dB same tube 19.94 mm 60 mm (2.36 in) 8.81 GHz 0.28 ≈96 dB 1/2 in Type L copper (ID 0.545 in) 13.84 mm 56 mm (2.2 in) 12.7 GHz 0.19 ≈129 dB Recommendation: a 3/4 in Type L copper tube 80 mm long, soldered all the way round (360°) into a copper plate (about 100×100 mm), which is soldered or taped into the wall. Add a 3/4 in copper end cap to close it. At 1296 MHz f/f_c = 0.15, and 433 MHz is further still below cutoff; the same length applies. IR note: Infrared passes straight through an open tube. It does not pass reliably through mesh or fabric, so don't aim the thermometer through the wall. The tube narrows the gun's view. Use a high distance-to-spot gun, or put the gun right against the tube mouth. Or use a battery temperature logger inside and read it after opening (no cable crosses the wall). HYP: "SLW passes the cage wall" is the SLW hypothesis, not established. The hole is also a test: take readings with the tube open and with it capped. CLASSICAL-TEM: at about 128 dB the tube adds essentially no ordinary-RF leakage, so a classical expectation is no difference between open and capped. transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis A difference would need explaining: first a leak or seam check, then an anomaly log. 8. Area, quantity and cost Area includes all 6 faces, a 50 mm (or 20 mm) overlap strip on each of the 12 edges, a 50 mm lid lip, and a 20% waste factor. Copper tape covers every seam on both sides plus the lid landing strip, with 20% waste. Cage Faces only With 50 mm seams + lip + 20% With 20 mm seams + lip + 20% Copper tape (both sides) 300 mm cube 0.54 m² 0.94 m² = 10.1 ft² 0.81 m² = 8.7 ft² 10.1 m = 33 ft 450 mm cube 1.22 m² 1.89 m² = 20.3 ft² 1.70 m² = 18.3 ft² 15.1 m = 50 ft 600 mm cube (Option 1) 2.16 m² 3.17 m² = 34.1 ft² 2.91 m² = 31.3 ft² 20.2 m = 66 ft 1000×600×600 mm (Option 2 / all-band) 3.12 m² 4.46 m² = 48.1 ft² 4.15 m² = 44.6 ft² 25.0 m = 82 ft 1300×650×650 mm 4.23 m² 5.93 m² = 63.8 ft² 5.55 m² = 59.8 ft² 29.6 m = 97 ft Cost (USD). "Verified" means the price was seen on the vendor page or listing on 2026-09-27. Everything else is an estimate. Item Option 1: 600 mm cube Option 2: 1000×600×600 Status Aluminium screen, Phifer 48 in × 25 ft (100 ft²) 1 roll, $41.55 1 roll, $41.55 verified (Home Depot) or 16-mesh copper, TWP, 36 in wide ~12 linear ft ~16–18 linear ft per-foot price unverified ("from $10") or Ni-Cu ripstop, Less EMF, 42.5 in ~10 ft ≈ $150 ~14 ft ≈ $209 "from $14.95/ft", verified listing Copper foil tape, conductive adhesive, 2 in × 33 ft (Vetco) 2 rolls = $41.90 3 rolls = $62.85 verified Frame: wood 1×2 or PVC plus corners ~$25–40 ~$35–55 unverified Door gasket or finger stock (or battens + clamps) ~$15–40 ~$20–50 unverified WBC tube: 3/4 in Type L copper (short length) + end cap + copper plate ~$15–25 ~$15–25 unverified Solder, zip ties, clamps ~$15 ~$15 unverified Total, aluminium screen ≈ $155–200 ≈ $190–250 mixed Total, Ni-Cu fabric ≈ $260–310 ≈ $360–420 mixed Total, copper mesh mesh price + ≈ $110–160 mesh price + ≈ $150–210 mesh price unverified 9. Build time for Steve (estimate) Task Option 1 (600 mm cube) Option 2 (1000×600×600) Build frame 1.5–2 h 2–3 h Cut and fit mesh panels 2–3 h 3–4 h Seams (solder or tape, both sides) 2–3 h 3–4 h Lid with lip and gasket or battens 1.5–2 h 2–3 h WBC tube and plate 1 h 1 h Leak check (below) 1 h 1 h Total ≈ 9–12 h ≈ 12–16 h Ni-Cu fabric bag with roll-top instead ≈ 3–5 h ≈ 4–6 h Leak check (CLASSICAL-TEM, simple): transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis Put the battery TinySA inside with the dipole. Record ambient Wi-Fi (2.4 GHz) and cell signals with the lid open. Close the lid, record again, then open and compare. The drop is a rough shielding figure. It is limited by the TinySA noise floor. 10. Cautions TinySA self-signal: in ULTRA mode (above 800 MHz) the TinySA leaks its local oscillator at up to −10 dBm out of the RF input (FACT, TinySA docs, noted earlier). In a sealed, reflective cage the dipole re-radiates this. Check with a 50 Ω load in place of the dipole, and enable spur suppression. Keep metal bodies back: the TinySA and the E5/H10 probe are metal objects too. Use the 300 mm coax to keep the TinySA in a corner, behind the dipole along the coax direction, not beside the rod. Safety: the cage is for receive only. Detectors, rods and the TinySA never go inside a running microwave oven. The hub's lab note ("Do not cook a sealed cage") applies if anything is ever transmitted inside.

description: Every equation the hub SLW simulators use, with its printed form, exact source (paper, equation, page), plain-English meaning and units of each symbol, which hub pages use it, and its status (FACT, HYP, ASSUMPTION or known typo with correction). Glossary and open questions.
text: Simulation Lab · equation source and meaning map · 2026-09-30 Equation source and meaning map for the SLW simulators For Dan's learning. Every equation the hub's SLW simulators use, with the equation as printed in its source, the exact source (paper, equation, page), what each symbol means in plain English with units, which hub pages use it, and whether it is FACT, HYP, ASSUMPTION or a known typo. MIXED ← Simulation Lab catalogue · Three readings of SLW loss · Joule-loss positions · Corrections log · P_OUT audit How to read this page. FACT = printed in the named source (equation, page or column given). HYP = Hively's SLW hypothesis or our inference. ASSUMPTION = a modelling choice made on a hub page. TYPO as printed = a known printing error, with the correction. DERIVED = algebra on printed equations. Where a symbol's definition is not in a source we have, the page says "not defined in the source we have" rather than guessing. Equations are taken only from the source files on the box (pdftotext of the papers and the notes recorded in the hub), not from memory. Under the SLW hypothesis no skin-depth, permeability or ferromagnetic argument is used; the allowed loss terms are Hively's Joule term σE∥² (2019 Eq. 44, as corrected by the 2019 erratum) or none (2022 Erratum). TEM reasoning is tagged transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis. The 2019 erratum PDF is private: its equations are cited, the PDF is neither embedded nor linked. Nobody has been contacted. Sources used Hively & Loebl 2019: L. M. Hively & A. S. Loebl, "Classical and extended electrodynamics", Phys. Essays 32, 112–126 (2019). Page numbers below are journal pages. 2019 erratum: Phys. Essays 32(3) 417 (2019), DOI 10.4006/0836-1398-32.3.417 (private copy; cited only). 2022 Erratum: Phys. Essays 35(3) 320 (2022), one page, as recorded in Joule-loss positions. Patent: L. M. Hively, US 9,306,527 B1 (2016). Keyport: US 12,525,711 B1. Hively & Land 2021: J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 1956, 012011. IARD 2020 slides (Hively & Land). Monstein & Wesley: Europhys. Lett. 59(4) 514–520 (2002). Butterworth et al.: J. Sci. Explor. 27(1) 13–23 (2013). Zimmerman: Mod. Phys. Lett. B 25(9) 649–662 (2011). Nikolova & Zimmerman: McMaster CEM-R-46 (2007). Meissner & Wentz: IEEE TGRS 42(9) 1836 (2004). Equations on this page Extended electrodynamics (EED) equations 18–22 C interface matching (Eq. 26) SLW drive and medium relation (Eq. 36 and the text after it) SLW impedance, Eq. (37) P_OUT, Eq. 38 / B5 as corrected by the 2019 erratum Patent US 9,306,527 B1, EQN. 15: radiated power Energy balance, Eq. (44) (and patent EQN. 14) Joule term σE∥² (what the hub uses as the allowed loss term) Hub Joule-literal attenuation αJ = σH|Z|/2 Charge relaxation E = E₀ exp(−σt/ε), τ = ε/σ 2022 Erratum: the SLW "is not subject to resistive loss" Transverse-EM comparison numbers (shown only as labelled reference) Monstein & Wesley scalar wave and flux, Eqs. (1)–(6) M&W wire-polarizer Joule loss, Eqs. (7)–(9) M&W ground-image signal model, Eqs. (10)–(14), (17), (18) M&W fitted amplitudes and reflection ratio, Eqs. (15)–(16), (19)–(24) M&W distance-loss term (p. 520): extra 1/e per 145 m Ranging equations on /ranging/ Radar cross-section (Mie, cylinder, optical, Rayleigh) on /slw-rcs/ Radar-range equations quoted on /sim-lab/scalar-wave-radar/ Seawater permittivity and conductivity (Meissner & Wentz 2004) Receiver-side potentials: Zimmerman, Nikolova–Zimmerman, Butterworth Keyport US 12,525,711 B1 (Navy SLW antenna) The equations Extended electrodynamics (EED) equations 18–22 FACT HYP E = −∇Φ − ∂A/∂t (18) B = ∇×A (19) C = ∇·A + (1/c²)∂Φ/∂t (20) ∇×B − (1/c²)∂E/∂t − ∇C = μJ (21) ∇·E + ∂C/∂t = ρ/ε (22) Source. Hively & Loebl, Phys. Essays 32, 112 (2019): Eqs. (18)–(22), p. 114 (charge density is printed "q" in the paper). Equation (20) is the definition of the scalar field C. The paper says "From Eq. (20), C has the same dimensions as B = μH" (p. 116). Symbol What it means (plain English) Units E electric field V/m B magnetic flux density T Φ scalar potential V A vector potential Wb/m = V·s/m C the scalar field of EED: the divergence of A plus (1/c²)∂Φ/∂t. In classical electrodynamics it is set to zero by the Lorenz gauge. In EED it is a real, dynamical field, and the paper says it has the dimensions of B T (same dimensions as B, p. 116) c speed of light in the medium, c = (εμ)−1/2 "not necessarily in vacuum" (p. 113) m/s J current density A/m² ρ (paper: q) free-charge density C/m³ ε, μ permittivity and permeability of the medium ("not necessarily vacuum", p. 113) F/m, H/m Hub pages that use it. Not computed directly. They are the starting point for Eq. 37, Eq. 38 and Eq. 44 below. Discussed on joule-loss-positions, submarine-slw-sources, experiment-g. Status: FACT as printed. HYP that the C field exists as a separate wave (this is the SLW hypothesis itself; not established physics). C interface matching (Eq. 26) FACT HYP (∇C/μ)₁ₙ = (∇C/μ)₂ₙ (26) Source. Hively & Loebl 2019, Eq. (26), p. 115: continuity of the normal component of ∇C/μ across an interface for long times; subscripts 1 and 2 are the two media. Symbol What it means (plain English) Units ∇C spatial gradient of the scalar field C T/m μ permeability of each medium H/m n normal component (perpendicular to the interface) – 1, 2 the two media on either side of the interface – Hub pages that use it. /slw-rcs/ (cited to say no reflection or transmission coefficient follows), scalar-wave-radar, submarine-slw-sources. This is the only interface condition for C in the source. No transmission or reflection coefficient, and no conductor boundary condition, is defined in the source we have. SLW drive and medium relation (Eq. 36 and the text after it) FACT HYP AL = ∇a ⟺ BT = 0 ⟺ JL = ∇κ (36); EL = JL/σ = ∇κ/σ; σ = ε₀ε″ω, ε = ε₀(ε′ − jε″) Source. Hively & Loebl 2019, Eq. (36) and the paragraph after it, p. 116. The text then says C, EL and JL "are all related by Eq. (32b) with σ = ε₀ε″ω and ε = ε₀(ε′ − jε″)". Symbol What it means (plain English) Units AL the longitudinal (irrotational, curl-free) part of A Wb/m a, κ scalar functions of space and time (their units are not stated in the source) – BT the transverse (solenoidal) magnetic part T JL, EL longitudinal (curl-free) current density and electric field: the SLW pieces A/m², V/m σ conductivity. Here the paper ties it to the imaginary part of the permittivity, σ = ε₀ε″ω, so it includes any dipolar loss. The hub calls this σH S/m ε′, ε″ real and imaginary parts of the relative permittivity – ω angular frequency 2πf rad/s Hub pages that use it. experiment-g, /slw-rcs/, sleeve-balun-snr (via σH in the Joule term), loss-modes. The paper argues no eddy currents form because ∇×EL = 0, so the SLW "is unimpeded by the skin effect". That is Hively's argument and is HYP. The hub does not use any skin-depth reasoning for the SLW. SLW impedance, Eq. (37) FACT HYP Z = |Er| / |C/(μ₀μ′)| = √(μ₀/ε₀) · √(μ′/ε′) · (1 − 1/(jkr)) / (1 − j tanδε) (37) Source. Hively & Loebl 2019, Eq. (37), p. 116; same form as Eq. Glossary SLW (scalar-longitudinal wave) In Hively's extended electrodynamics (EED), a wave made of the longitudinal electric field EL and the scalar field C, with no magnetic field (B = 0). A hypothesis, not established physics. EED / CED Extended electrodynamics (Hively's theory, with the C field) versus classical electrodynamics (Maxwell's equations with the Lorenz gauge, C = 0). C field The scalar field defined by Eq. (20): C = ∇·A + (1/c²)∂Φ/∂t. Same dimensions as B. Zero in classical theory, dynamical in EED. Irrotational / longitudinal A field with zero curl (∇×F = 0). The SLW's EL and JL are curl-free. Joule term (J·E = σE∥²) Power per volume that the electric field delivers to conduction current. The allowed SLW loss term on this hub. E∥ The electric field component parallel to the current or wire. Each hub page defines it locally; Hively does not define it for the SLW. σ, ε, τ Conductivity (S/m), permittivity (F/m) and relaxation time τ = ε/σ (s). Loss tangent tanδ ε″/ε′, the ratio of the lossy to the lossless part of the permittivity. Np/m and dB/m Attenuation units. 1 Np = 8.686 dB for a field amplitude. A field falling as exp(−αr) loses power as exp(−2αr). P_OUT Hively's "power output" from a monopole, Eq. 38/B5. On the hub: a power density in W/m² at range r. Null / image source A distance at which the direct and the ground-reflected waves cancel. M&W treat the ground as producing an image of the source. RCS (radar cross-section) The equivalent area that would give the same echo if it re-radiated equally in all directions. FACT / HYP / ASSUMPTION FACT: taken from a source with equation and page. HYP: Hively's SLW hypothesis or our inference. ASSUMPTION: a modelling choice on a hub page. TEM Transverse electromagnetic wave (ordinary radio). Any TEM reasoning on the hub is tagged "transverse-EM reasoning, NOT applicable under the SLW hypothesis". Symbols and quantities flagged "not defined in the source we have" Item What is missing Note I (Eq. 38, B5, patent 15) whether peak or rms 2019 paper, 2019 erratum and patent say only "the current". The hub's peak is an ASSUMPTION (Dan, 2026-09-30). E∥ for the SLW which field component, and in which geometry Not defined in any Hively text. Defined page by page on the hub. α in patent EQN. 13 the quantity α in C/Er = (ε′/c)(1+jα)/(1+j/kr) Partly unreadable in our scan of US 9,306,527. The surrounding text contrasts a low-conductivity medium and a good conductor. per-metre SLW attenuation any α for the SLW No Hively source gives one. αJ is a hub construction. source of the ρC/(εμ) energy where the power-source term gets its energy Not quantified in any Hively source. units of Φ, q, A, B, S in M&W unit system Not stated (Gaussian-like forms suggest Gaussian, HYP). σ of brass in M&W conductivity of the wires Not given; κ = 4.4 is fitted. M&W ground-loss mechanism Earth σ, current path, onset distance Not given: no equation, no σ; onset "beyond 100 m" (Butterworth: about 200 m). 1.3/fGHz factor in the hub Az origin of the frequency dependence Not found in Zimmerman's text. Hub construction. SLW reflection or conductor boundary condition any transmission or reflection law for C Only the Eq. 26 matching condition exists. μ′ in Eq. 37 how to treat a non-vacuum μ′ The paper says μ′ is "not necessarily vacuum". The hub uses 1 and makes no permeability argument. Keyport equations any equation None in the text we have. a, κ in Eq. 36 units of the scalar functions Not stated in the source. Questions I still have For Dan to decide what, if anything, to ask the authors later. Nobody has been contacted and none of these has been sent to anyone. Is I in Eq. 38 / B5 the peak or the rms current? How does the 2022 Erratum's "not subject to resistive loss" relate to the J·E term that stays in Eq. 44? Is the cancellation an exchange of energy, and where does the replenishing energy come from (the ρC/(εμ) term)? Is M&W's extra 1/e-per-145 m loss beyond about 100 m an SLW loss, or a classical ground or return-current effect (Hively & Loebl App. D mention unquantified ground currents)? Does the charge-relaxation time τ = ε/σ map onto any received-signal factor, and if so which time t (source, travel, detector)? What is the definition of α in patent EQN. 13? Does the C-field matching condition (Eq. 26) give any reflection or transmission at a conductor? Patent Eq. 15 total I²Z₀/(4π) is twice the erratum total I²Z₀/(8π). Which does the author intend for the radiated power? Should σ in the Joule term include the dipolar part (σH = ε₀ε″ω, Eq. 36 text), or only dc conduction? What is E∥ for the SLW in a conducting medium, in Hively's formalism? Are the raw Fig. 5 data points from M&W (2002) available? Related: three readings of SLW loss (interactive).
